items.title: Operation Identity Evidence Archive: 8 Synthetic Cases
items.abstract: Operation Identity Evidence Archive is an original offline educational software package for reviewing a saved operation identity after an ambiguous result. It keeps the request, assumed dispatch and unresolved or assumed result evidence separate. Every output retains retry_authorized: false. Contents and reproduction Version 1.0.0 contains a Python standard-library checker, an explicit eleven-field contract, a JSON schema, eight synthetic fixtures and eight retained expected reports. The archive also includes a local test suite, a reproduction command, source references and file checksums. No dependency installation is required. Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v, then python3 reproduce.py from the extracted package directory. The second command compares all eight generated reports with retained bytes. Run python3 evidence.py fixtures/01-unresolved.json to inspect a single report. Invalid input exits 2 without a success-shaped result. Method and verification boundary The checker compares a saved fingerprint with a specified compact, sorted-key Python JSON representation of the synthetic request. It collects all evidence gaps and applies ordered review gates for missing identity, absent pre-dispatch evidence, unresolved results and missing result references. An unestablished dispatch never becomes proof that an operation did not occur. Local verification covers the authored behavior and all 72 combinations of the specified dispatch, result, reference, pre-dispatch-record and reviewer states. The eight fixtures demonstrate individual gates and combined gaps. This is verification of a local educational model, not an external API, provider, client system or recovery process. No network operation or retry was performed. A matching request fingerprint does not authenticate a record or guarantee deduplication across concurrent requests. A result reference in a fixture is an invented premise, not a completed provider lookup. Even a recorded-result review state grants no permission to repeat an effect. The exact serialization profile and assumptions are documented in CONTRACT.md. Provenance, rights and context Prepared by Dmytro Nasyrov, affiliated with Pharos Production. AI assisted preparation, implementation and root technical review. No independent human review or peer review is claimed. All operation IDs, requests and result references are synthetic. The background reference is the Amazon Builders' Library discussion of idempotent APIs. It explains the importance of request identity when a response is missing. The archive's schema and gate ordering are authored choices, not an AWS-prescribed standard. The affiliated engineering context is Pharos Production AI agent development. The public service description is not evidence of client deployment or performance for this artifact. The original code, documentation and synthetic fixtures are licensed under MIT. The official company logo is excluded and remains its owner's property. External source pages are referenced, not redistributed. Python 3.10 or later is required; execution was checked with Python 3.14.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: One Leak Away: How Pretrained Model Exposure Amplifies Jailbreak Risks in Finetuned LLMs
items.abstract: Finetuning pretrained large language models (LLMs) has become the standard paradigm for developing downstream applications. However, its security implications remain unclear, particularly regarding whether finetuned LLMs inherit jailbreak vulnerabilities from their pretrained sources. We investigate this question in a realistic pretrain-to-finetune threat model, where an attacker has full access to a released pretrained LLM but no access to its proprietary finetuned derivatives. Empirical analysis shows that adversarial prompts optimized on the pretrained model transfer most effectively to its finetuned variants, revealing inherited vulnerabilities from pretrained to finetuned LLMs. To further examine this inheritance, we conduct representation-level probing, which shows that transferable prompts are linearly separable within the pretrained hidden states, suggesting that transferability-relevant structure is already encoded in pretrained representations. Building on this insight, we propose the Probe-Guided Projection (PGP) attack, which steers optimization toward transferability-relevant directions. Experiments across multiple LLM families and diverse finetuned tasks confirm PGP's strong transfer success, underscoring the security risks inherent in the pretrain-to-finetune paradigm. Finally, we demonstrate that the same representation-level insights also enable a lightweight defense that mitigates pretrain-to-finetune jailbreak transfer while preserving downstream utility.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Nb2O5 Interlayer Engineering for Switchable Polarization and Tunneling Electroresistance in HZO-Based Ferroelectric Tunnel Junctions
items.abstract: Abstract Hf1–xZrxO2 (HZO)-based ferroelectric tunnel junctions (FTJs) enable polarization-controlled resistance switching at nanometer-scale thicknesses, offering potential for nonvolatile memory and multilevel conductance operation. In metal–ferroelectric–insulator–ferroelectric–metal (MFIFM) structures, highly insulating interlayers such as Al2O3 can suppress leakage at the expense of switchable polarization and low-resistance-state (LRS) transport. Here, Nb2O5 is explored as an alternative interlayer with a relatively low electron-transport barrier, and Al2O3- and Nb2O5-inserted MFIFM FTJs with identical HZO layer thicknesses and total dielectric-stack thicknesses are directly compared. Replacing Al2O3 with Nb2O5 increases the positive-up–negative-down (PUND)-derived 2Pr from 17.2 to 27.4 μC/cm2, accompanied by a higher fitted orthorhombic-phase contribution and a higher out-of-plane texture index. The Nb2O5-inserted device also exhibits a higher tunneling electroresistance (TER) ratio than its Al2O3-inserted counterpart (60 vs 36 at a read voltage of 1.2 V), accompanied by a larger relative increase in LRS current than in high-resistance-state (HRS) current. The Nb2O5-inserted device further exhibits a higher breakdown voltage than the Al2O3-inserted counterpart, maintains distinguishable polarization states up to approximately 107 switching cycles, and demonstrates repeatable overall multilevel conductance-update behavior over 20 consecutive cycles, despite variations in individual intermediate conductance levels. These results establish interlayer selection as an effective strategy for modulating switchable polarization, resistance-state transport, and electrical reliability in HZO-based MFIFM FTJs.

items.title: NVBleed: Covert and Side-Channel Attacks on NVIDIA Multi-GPU Interconnect
items.abstract: Multi-GPU systems are becoming increasingly important in highperformance computing (HPC) and cloud infrastructure, providing acceleration for data-intensive applications, including machine learning workloads. These systems consist of multiple GPUs interconnected through high-speed networking links such as NVIDIA's NVLink. In this work, we explore whether the interconnect on such systems can offer a novel source of leakage, enabling new forms of covert and side-channel attacks. Specifically, we reverse engineer the operations of NVlink and identify two primary sources of leakage: timing variations due to contention and accessible performance counters that disclose communication patterns. The leakage is visible remotely and even across VM instances in the cloud, enabling potentially dangerous attacks. Building on these observations, we develop two types of covert-channel attacks across two GPUs, achieving a bandwidth of over 70 Kbps with an error rate of 4.78% for the contention channel. We develop two end-to-end crossGPU side-channel attacks: application fingerprinting (including 18 high-performance computing and deep learning applications) and 3D graphics character identification within Blender, a multi-GPU rendering application. These attacks are highly effective, achieving F1 scores of up to 97.78% and 91.56%, respectively. We also discover that leakage surprisingly occurs across Virtual Machines on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) and demonstrate a side-channel attack on Blender, achieving F1 scores exceeding 88%. We also explore potential defenses such as managing access to counters and reducing the resolution of the clock to mitigate the two sources of leakage.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
items.abstract: Large foundation models are integrated into Computer Use Agents (CUAs), enabling autonomous interaction with operating systems through graphical user interfaces (GUIs) to perform complex tasks. This autonomy introduces serious security risks: malicious instructions or visual prompt injections can trigger unsafe reasoning and cause harmful system-level actions. Existing defenses, such as detection-based blocking, prevent damage but often abort tasks prematurely, reducing agent utility. In this paper, we present MirrorGuard, a plug-and-play defense framework that uses simulation-based training to improve CUA security in the real world. To reduce the cost of large-scale training in operating systems, we propose a novel neural-symbolic simulation pipeline, which generates realistic, high-risk GUI interaction trajectories entirely in a text-based simulated environment, which captures unsafe reasoning patterns and potential system hazards without executing real operations. In the simulation environment, MirrorGuard learns to intercept and rectify insecure reasoning chains of CUAs before they produce and execute unsafe actions. In real-world testing, extensive evaluations across diverse benchmarks and CUA architectures show that MirrorGuard significantly mitigates security risks. For instance, on the ByteDance UI-TARS system, it reduces the unsafe rate from 66.5% to 13.0% while maintaining a marginal false refusal rate (FRR). In contrast, the state-of-the-art GuardAgent only achieves a reduction to 53.9% and suffers from a 15.4% higher FRR. Our work proves that simulation-derived defenses can provide robust, real-world protection while maintaining the fundamental utility of the agent. Our code and model are publicly available at https://bmz-q-q.github.io/MirrorGuard/.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
items.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems enhance LLMs with external knowledge but introduce a critical attack surface: corpus poisoning. While recent studies have demonstrated the potential of such attacks, they typically rely on impractical assumptions, such as white-box access or known user queries, thereby underestimating the difficulty of real-world exploitation. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proposing MIRAGE, a novel multi-stage poisoning pipeline designed for strict black-box and query-agnostic environments. Operating on surrogate model feedback, MIRAGE functions as an automated optimization framework that integrates three key mechanisms: it utilizes persona-driven query synthesis to approximate latent user search distributions, employs semantic anchoring to imperceptibly embed these intents for high retrieval visibility, and leverages an adversarial variant of Test-Time Preference Optimization (TPO) to maximize persuasion. To rigorously evaluate this threat, we construct a new benchmark derived from three long-form, domain-specific datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that MIRAGE significantly outperforms existing baselines in both attack efficacy and stealthiness, exhibiting remarkable transferability across diverse retriever-LLM configurations and highlighting the urgent need for robust defense strategies.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Identification automatique de domaines de connaissances dans un dictionnaire universel du XVIIIe s.
items.abstract: On se propose de présenter les résultats d’une recherche visant à l’identification et à la classification automatique de domaines de connaissances dans un dictionnaire universel du XVIIIe siècle.L’œuvre support des analyses est l’édition de 1743 du Dictionnaire Universel François & Latin (désormais, DUFLT) dit de Trévoux. Environ 20 % des articles héberge un ou plusieurs paragraphes associés à une marque de domaine (Pétrequin 2009, Turcan 2024) qui stipule de quelle science (astronomie ...), art (poësie ... forge...) ou métier (charron ...) relève le contenu. On est loin de la systématicité de l’Encyclopédie de Diderot et d’Alembert (1751-1772) où 83% environ des articles est pourvu d’une marque de domaine (données tirées de l’ARTFL et de l’ENCCRE). Notre objectif est de parvenir à une classification complète de l’ensemble des paragraphes du dictionnaire en leur affectant un ou plusieurs domaines de connaissance. Pour ce faire, nous développons une approche combinant grands modèles de langage (LLMs) et modèles de classification supervisée. On soulignera que la classification en domaines de connaissances a déjà fait l’objet de plusieurs études computationnelles sur l’Encyclopédie de Diderot & d’Alembert (Horton et al. 2009, Roe et al. 2016, Brenon et al. 2022), mais qu’aucune n’a été conduite à ce jour sur le DUFLT.Dans une première partie, nous présenterons les choix méthodologiques qui structurent notre démarche. Nous justifierons le choix du paragraphe comme unité de base de nos analyses, le regroupement des marques de domaine (simples : en termes de géographie ...; complexes : Terme de Botanique & de Pharmacie) en un nombre restreint de « macro-domaines ». Nous aborderons également les difficultés liées à l’hétérogénéité de ces marques et à la nature parfois pluri-/inter-disciplinaire de leurs contenus.Dans une seconde partie, nous décrirons le protocole expérimental mis en œuvre. À partir d’un ensemble de paragraphes initialement pourvus d’une ou plusieurs marques de domaine (que l’on aura retirées), nous sollicitons différents LLMs dans un cadre de classification few-shot afin de leur faire associer un ou plusieurs macro-domaines. Les prédictions sont ensuite évaluées par comparaison avec les annotations existantes. Cette phase permet d’identifier les configurations de prompts et les modèles les plus performants, et d’affiner progressivement les instructions fournies aux modèles. Les résultats préliminaires montrent qu’un des modèles testés (Gemini 3.5 Flash) atteint un F-score proche de 70 % sur un jeu d’évaluation encore limité à une cinquantaine de paragraphes. L’extension de ce jeu de test constitue une étape importante afin d’obtenir une mesure plus robuste des performances.Le meilleur modèle sera ensuite appliqué à un ensemble de paragraphes dépourvus de marque de domaine. Les annotations produites feront l’objet d’une validation et d’une correction manuelle, permettant la constitution d’un corpus de référence (gold standard). Ce corpus servira à l’entraînement d’un modèle de classification supervisée fondé sur une architecture Transformer de type encodeur, mieux adaptée à un déploiement à grande échelle sur l’ensemble du dictionnaire.Nous montrerons que cette approche progressive, associant annotation assistée par LLM et apprentissage supervisé, permet non seulement d’améliorer la couverture de l’annotation thématique du DUFLT, mais aussi d’ouvrir de nouvelles perspectives pour l’étude de l’organisation des savoirs dans les dictionnaires encyclopédiques du XVIIIe siècle.

items.title: Hoss: Fast Oblivious Semantic Search with Heterogeneous GPU-CPU-TEE Architecture
items.abstract: Semantic search is widely deployed in modern AI systems, but protecting both data contents and access patterns remains challenging. The current state-of-the-art system, Compass, achieves oblivious semantic search by building an optimized ORAM over HNSW graphs. However, even with aggressive optimizations, it still incurs large overheads. Closing this performance gap is fundamentally difficult: Compass has already removed most cryptographic overheads, leaving ORAM accesses as the dominant cost, which are constrained by well-known Omega(log N) bandwidth lower bounds. Our key insight is that traditional ORAM overhead stems from the assumption of limited private memory, whereas modern GPU TEEs provide large private memory (Pmem) that blinds internal access patterns (Hunt et al., NSDI '23). This shift opens a new design space. We therefore propose Hoss, a first-of-its-kind oblivious semantic search system with a heterogeneous CPU-GPU TEE architecture that supports fast, scalable search with low cost of ownership. In Hoss, the GPU TEE's large Pmem hosts the hot-path HNSW traversal, while the lower layers of the graph, if they exceed GPU capacity, are offloaded to CPU TEEs. The system invokes oblivious primitives only when accessing these lower layers. The availability of large Pmem also enables new optimization opportunities. For example, Hoss features a host-access ORAM mechanism that goes beyond traditional performance constraints and incorporates several data-dependent optimizations that are not possible in prior designs. We implement a prototype of Hoss and benchmark it against Compass. Our results show that Hoss achieves up to 67x speedup while maintaining high recall, with larger gains at scale.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Heterogeneous Memristive Neuromorphic Computing with Physics-Aware Cross-Modal Attention for Energy-Efficient Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) is a crucial technology for achieving emotional intelligence in human–computer interaction. However, the substantial computational demands of MER models currently overwhelm the capacities of resource-constrained edge devices. To address this problem, this paper proposes a Heterogeneous Memristive Neural Network for Multimodal Emotion Recognition. The proposed network adopts a hardware–algorithm co-design approach, in which different memristive devices are assigned to different modal processing tasks according to their physical characteristics. Specifically, highly stable filamentary memristors are utilized to construct deterministic feature extraction pathways for text and video, whereas highly plastic Phase-Change Memory (PCM) crossbar arrays are designed for audio encoding. Based on the high plasticity of PCM, a memristive cross-modal attention network is further designed to achieve dynamic and adaptive multimodal feature fusion. Furthermore, a collaborative weight update method is proposed. During weight updates, the inherent writing noise and conductance drift of PCM are utilized as hardware-level regularization and automatic sparse learning strategies. Simulation experiments conducted on the IEMOCAP and MELD datasets using the MemTorch framework demonstrate that the proposed neural network maintains recognition accuracy comparable to GPU baseline models, even when accounting for device non-idealities. Overall, the proposed neural network effectively resolves the “performance–power” conflict when deploying high-performance MER models on resource-constrained edge devices, providing an efficient and stable neuromorphic computing solution for edge applications.

items.title: Flexible Low-Voltage Thin-Film Transistors for Logic Circuits and Neuromorphic Computing Applications
items.abstract: Flexible thin-film transistors (TFTs) operating at low voltage are key building blocks for next-generation wearable electronics and brain-inspired systems, yet simultaneously achieving low-voltage operation, environmental robustness and multifunctionality remains a great challenge. In this work, flexible indium gallium zinc oxide (IGZO) TFTs based on a solution-processed nanocomposite gate dielectric were fabricated, in which the introduced nanofiller effectively enhanced the capacitance, mechanical strength and moisture resistance of the polymer dielectric. The resulting devices exhibit an on/off ratio over 106 and can be fully turned on at a gate voltage below 1 V. After 2000 bending cycles, 90-day ambient aging and 3600 s continuous gate-bias stress, the threshold voltage and subthreshold swing show only slight drifts and the on/off ratio remains above 106, demonstrating outstanding mechanical durability, anti-aging capability and bias stability. On this basis, a logic inverter was constructed, which delivers a peak voltage gain of ~9 at a supply voltage of 2.5 V and realizes stable dynamic inversion for low-frequency square-wave signals. Owing to the tunable ion migration and electric double-layer polarization of the gate dielectric, the TFTs emulate typical biological synaptic behaviors, including pulse-dependent potentiation, long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). Neural network simulations based on device conductance states achieve accuracy of ~90% on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset and 88.1% on the challenging Stanford Cars vehicle dataset. This work verifies that the developed flexible TFTs possess dual functions of logic operation and neuromorphic computing, providing a feasible solution for the development of high-performance flexible low-power electronic devices and brain-inspired vision systems.

items.title: First-principles investigation of small polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3
items.abstract: Sodium niobate ( NaNbO 3 ) is a perovskite oxide and a key component of emerging lead-free antiferroelectric capacitors for high-energy-density applications. However, its performance can be hindered by irreversible phase transitions and leakage currents associated with low electrical resistivity. Defect and doping engineering offers a potential way to overcome these problems, but its use requires a detailed understanding of electronic, ionic, and polaron charge-compensation mechanisms, where the role of polarons remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the stability of small hole and electron polarons in rhombohedral NaNbO 3 , which is a structurally well-defined model system that avoids lattice-dynamical instabilities. Trapping energies are calculated using density functional theory corrected by a Hubbard U , using the enforced-piecewise-linearity approach including finite-size scaling. For the small hole-polaron centered on O- 2 p orbital, we find a trapping energy of − 0.65 eV and an adiabatic migration barrier of 0.32 eV determined by nudged-elastic-band calculations. In contrast, we show that excess electrons do not self-trap on Nb- 4 d orbitals, reflecting weak electron-phonon coupling in the conduction band manifold. These results identify oxygen as an intrinsic hole trap in NaNbO 3 and highlight the importance of including hole polarons in defect models of NaNbO 3 -based electroceramics.

items.title: Enhancement of the Mechanical Properties of Low-k SiCOH Films by Plasma Treatment and Ultraviolet Curing
items.abstract: The integration of organosilicate SiCOH low-k dielectrics in back-end-of-line (BEOL) interconnect structures requires a balance between low k and sufficient mechanical robustness. Low-k films with a thickness of approximately 2800 Å were deposited on 300 mm Si wafers via plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) using diethoxymethylsilane (DEMS) and O2 at 260 °C. To investigate the effects of process engineering on film properties, the total film thickness was divided into one, two, three, five, or 10 sublayers to compare segmentation, cyclic O2/He-plasma treatment, and interleaved ultraviolet (UV) curing. The resulting films were characterized by spectroscopic ellipsometry, nanoindentation, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) depth profiles, and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy. Segmentation increased the k value from 3.35 to 3.66, accompanied by a non-monotonic mechanical response. Extending the plasma treatment from 1 to 20 s led to a 19.8% rise in the k value, along with respective increases of 9.4% in hardness and 16.1% in the modulus, consistent with carbon/hydride removal and oxidative densification of the silicate network. Increasing RF power from 300 to 900 W caused smaller dielectric changes while raising the hardness and modulus by 8.7% and 10.6%, respectively, indicating diminishing changes at higher applied powers. Interleaved UV curing, comprising UV irradiation and concurrent thermal treatment, reduced the thickness, increased the refractive index (RI), and maintained a lower k relative to the as-deposited films. After five UV curing cycles, the hardness and modulus reached the highest mean values of 4.6 GPa and 35.8 GPa, respectively. FTIR analysis showed systematic depletion of Si–CH3 and Si–H groups and Si–O–Si network evolution, whereas XPS showed relatively stable plateau composition but treatment-sensitive transition regions. The combined results are consistent with oxidation-related modification during plasma treatment and network reorganization during UV curing, with possible differences in the spatial extent of these processes. These results further indicate that an intermediate cycle count provides a favorable balance between dielectric and mechanical properties.

items.title: Electric-Field-Driven Surface Ionic Transport on Hydroxylated SiO2 Governs Transient Leakage and Hybrid Bonding Reliability
items.abstract: Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding is critical for 3D integrated circuit packaging, where dielectric surface activation impacts bonding quality and long-term reliability. NaOH-based wet chemical activation is a promising approach for a scalable and cost-effective processing under ambient conditions. However, this route introduces residual ions at the SiO2 surface, raising concerns regarding electrical leakage and dielectric stability. In this study, electric-field-driven surface ionic transport on NaOH-activated SiO2 and its role in transient leakage and hybrid bonding reliability were investigated. Reversible and polarity-dependent transient current peaks observed in cyclic electrical measurements provide evidence for electric-field-driven migration of the mobile ionic species at the SiO2 interface. In addition, higher NaOH concentrations promoted greater residual Na+ accumulation and intensified transient leakage peaks, supporting the selection of 0.5 M NaOH as an effective activation condition. Systematic decoupling experiments demonstrate that residual mobile Na+ ions are the dominant contributors to the transient leakage current rather than fixed hydroxyl groups. Quantitative analysis reveals Na+ surface mobility of approximately 3 × 10-10 m2V-1s-1, an order-of-magnitude upper-bound estimate that is consistent between constant-bias and ramped-bias measurements and about six orders of magnitude higher than that in bulk SiO2, suggesting a surface-dominated transport. An optimized 3 min deionized water (DI) rinse reduces the mobile Na+ population below the electrical detection limit and decreases the Na 1s XPS intensity by roughly an order of magnitude, suppressing the transient leakage to near-baseline levels while maintaining hydrophilicity and achieving the SiO2-SiO2 bonding strength of 19.7 ± 1.8 MPa, comparable to Ar plasma activation. The leakage measurements were performed on Cu/SiO2 damascene comb structures, whereas the bonding validation addresses the dielectric part of the hybrid-bonding interface; Cu-Cu contact and long-term stress testing remain to be verified. This work provides a framework for understanding electric-field-driven surface ionic transport and practical guidelines for contamination control of the dielectric surface in wet-activated Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding.

items.title: Development and validation of a scale assessing perceived trustworthiness in large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly part of everyday life, yet there is no established way to measure how users evaluate their trustworthiness. This study introduces the Perceived Trustworthiness of LLMs scale (PT-LLM-8), a self-report psychometric instrument measuring users’ perceived trustworthiness of their primary LLM. PT-LLM-8 is developed from the TrustLLM framework and adapted as a human-centred measure. The PT-LLM-8 comprises eight items representing truthfulness, safety, fairness, robustness, privacy, transparency, accountability, and compliance with laws. Psychometric properties of the scale were tested with 752 LLM users in the United Kingdom (Mean age = 28.58, SD = 6.11, 50.3% males, 48.8% females). Exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses supported a one-factor structure, with high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.90, Composite Reliability = 0.91, strong item-total correlations (ranged between 0.62 and 0.75), and measurement invariance across gender. The total score measures overall perceived trustworthiness, while individual item responses may also be examined descriptively for information about the content represented by each item. For researchers, practitioners, and developers, the PT-LLM-8 offers a practical instrument for evaluating interventions, comparing groups and contexts, and examining whether technical safeguards are reflected in users’ perceived trustworthiness of LLM. The scale can also be applied to guide system design, support policy development, and help organisations monitor shifts in user trust toward LLMs over time, making it applicable across research, practice, and governance.

items.title: Deterministic Agentic Workflows and Cognitive Enterprise Search Framework (2026)
items.abstract: This technical report outlines the architectural paradigms required to deploy autonomous AI agents and enterprise cognitive search systems within strict corporate governance parameters. While large language models demonstrate high conversational capability, enterprise adoption requires deterministic tool execution, verifiable grounding, and full EU AI Act compliance. Enterprise AI consulting and operational frameworks are provided by Heinrich Co, developing tailored intelligence roadmaps for global institutions. 1. Cognitive Search & Enterprise Knowledge Synthesis Conventional keyword retrieval systems fail to capture semantic relationships across distributed corporate repositories. Implementing hybrid vector embeddings alongside deterministic BM25 lexical search enables context-aware discovery without hallucination risks. Review implementation details in AI Powered Enterprise Search. 2. AI Readiness & Corporate Operational Audits Successful AI transformation requires data hygiene, schema standardization, and organizational alignment. Before deploying autonomous agent pipelines, enterprises must assess infrastructure feasibility. Reference the structured framework in AI Readiness Consulting Assessment Deliverables. 3. Executive Governance and Future-Proof Roadmaps Strategic deployment must balance rapid innovation with ethical risk management and regulatory accountability. Learn more in the executive analysis Foreword Blog En.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Data-Driven Estimation of Ship Manoeuvring Hydrodynamic Derivatives using a Hybrid MARUS–PINN Framework with LLM-Guided Symbolic Discovery
items.abstract: Identification of hydrodynamic derivatives that govern ship manoeuvring behaviour for autonomous vessels such as unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) is essential for diverse maritime purposes including oceanographic research, environmental monitoring, and autonomous navigation. However, conventional hydrodynamic modelling approaches, such as classical manoeuvring models, experimental methods, and high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics (CFD), are often labour-intensive, costly, and time-consuming, and their estimated parameters may not fully capture real-world operating conditions due to nonlinearities, scale effects, and complex sea states. With the advent of machine learning, recent advances in Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) offer a promising alternative by embedding governing fluid-dynamic equations directly into the neural learning network, providing the advantages of data-driven learning while maintaining physical consistency. Hence, this thesis investigates a novel approach that combines Marine Robotics Unity Simulator (MARUS)–simulated manoeuvring data, PINN-based parameter learning, and symbolic discovery via Large Language Models (LLMs) to estimate hydrodynamic derivatives with improved robustness, reduced data requirements, and enhanced interpretability compared to conventional system identification methods, while promoting interoperability and standardization through its modular design. To evaluate this hybrid approach, the thesis addresses the following research question: Can a hybrid MARUS–PINN–LLM framework provide more accurate, interpretable, and data-efficient estimates of manoeuvring hydrodynamic derivatives than conventional system identification methods? To this end, an extensive set of experiments and ablation studies is conducted to compare the proposed hybrid model with its purely data-driven and purely physics-based counterparts across parameter accuracy, trajectory reconstruction quality, and generalization to diverse maneuvering conditions of various industry-standard USVs. The results demonstrate that integrating symbolic discovery with PINNs reduces sway-acceleration error by 86%, yaw-rate acceleration error by 66%, and heading-rollout error by 89% relative to purely data-driven baselines, producing compact, physically consistent residual terms that align with established nonlinear hydrodynamic effects while its physics-only counterparts catastrophically diverge from the ground-truths. Taken together, these findings highlight the potential of hybrid physics–machine-learning frameworks to advance the estimation of manoeuvring coefficients for the next generation of autonomous marine systems.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via Token-wise Representation Editing and Residual Fusion
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into IT infrastructures, where they process user data according to predefined instructions. However, conventional LLMs remain vulnerable to prompt injection, where malicious users inject directive tokens into the data to subvert model behavior. Existing defenses train LLMs to semantically separate data and instruction tokens, but still struggle to (1) balance utility and security and (2) prevent instruction-like semantics in the data from overriding the intended instructions. We propose DRIP, which (1) precisely removes instruction semantics from tokens in the data section while preserving their data semantics, and (2) robustly preserves the effect of the intended instruction even under strong adversarial content. To "de-instructionalize" data tokens, DRIP introduces a data curation and training paradigm with a lightweight representation-editing module that edits embeddings of instruction-like tokens in the data section, enhancing security without harming utility. To ensure non-overwritability of instructions, DRIP adds a minimal residual module that reduces the ability of adversarial data to overwrite the original instruction. We evaluate DRIP on LLaMA 8B and Mistral 7B against StruQ, SecAlign, ISE, and PFT on three prompt-injection benchmarks (SEP, AlpacaFarm, and InjecAgent). DRIP improves role-separation score by 12-49\%, reduces attack success rate by over 66\% under adaptive attacks, and matches the utility of the undefended model, establishing a new state of the art for prompt-injection robustness.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: DDRop: Active Memory Interposer Attacks on Confidential VMs by Dropping DDR5 Writes
items.abstract: Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) are increasingly deployed in the cloud to protect sensitive workloads through hardware-enforced isolation, remote attestation, and transparent memory encryption. However, to meet memory performance and size demands, modern TEEs omit cryptographic freshness guarantees, leaving them vulnerable to replay attacks by adversaries with physical memory access. Prior work demonstrated low-cost active interposition attacks on DDR4 without requiring expensive specialized equipment, but these techniques do not extend to DDR5, where existing approaches are limited to passive ciphertext side-channel analysis and rely on bus downclocking to accommodate legacy memory bus analyzers. We present the first low-cost (<200$) DDR5 RDIMM interposer capable of active fault injection at native speeds. By injecting targeted parity errors to silently discard cache line writebacks, we introduce DDRop, a new primitive that exploits the absence of cryptographic freshness to break the integrity of Intel TDX, Scalable SGX, and AMD SEV-SNP. Building on this primitive and targeting the APIs exposed by the TDX module and AMD Secure Processor, we show that adversaries can gain ciphertext access, copy arbitrary victim pages, and inject malicious secure page-table entries. We demonstrate end-to-end attacks on an up-to-date TDX platform, including forcing any TD into debug mode and forging attestation reports. While software-level mitigations, including timing-based interposer detection and API hardening, may reduce the attack surface, our results demonstrate that active DDR5 bus interposition is practical at low cost, highlighting the need for robust cryptographic memory integrity protections against physical adversaries.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Conserved amount, negotiable placement. Prompting perturbs one architecture, an AI reviewer both
items.abstract: Tesler's conservation law holds that a problem carries an irreducible amount of complexity. Brooks separates that essential part from the accidental part a solution adds. If the essential part is fixed, architecture is placement rather than quantity, and the question is which levers move placement. An AI agent implements sixty accumulating change requests on one REST endpoint under two architectures, a mutative Spring controller and an additive OfficeFloor pipeline, under five conditions, ten runs per cell, model fixed. Four are external controls, from a bare change request to the disclosed structural cost function. The fifth is different in kind. A second agent reviews each change and reasons about cohesion itself. Amount is steady. Across all ten cells the finished complexity varies by 7% to 20% over four operationalisations, and the complexity the sixty rules added by 21% to 29% within an architecture. Strict correctness fell in most comparisons though each rule was implemented correctly in over 99% of checkpoints, and all three outcome measures favour the concentrated codebase. The contribution is a measurable property of an architecture and its lever, not a verdict on either.

items.title: CNTFET Based Low Power SRAM Design: Architectures, Challenges and Innovative Implementations
items.abstract: Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) takes on a vital role in digital technology especially for applications that demand high speed and low power consumption. However, there are top priority with leakage power, reliability and stability owing to continuous technological advancement and the demand for energy efficient systems. Thorough research of low power SRAM design approaches is presented with an emphasis on cutting edge cell topologies and innovative device technologies. Power efficiency, read/write stability and area overhead are examined for various SRAM designs including 6T, 7T, 8T, 9T and 10T cells. Special attention is focused on SRAM designs using Carbon Nanotube Field Effect Transistor (CNTFET) which provide excellent electrical characteristics and less leakage than conventional silicon enabled methods. Subthreshold operation and assist methods that enable ultra low voltage capability are also included in the article. To further emphasize the need of low power SRAM designs, growing application domains like Internet of Things (IoT), biomedical systems and Compute-In-Memory architectures are investigated. Major performance deals and design trends are identified through a comparative analysis of this research. In order to facilitate growth of next generation low power SRAM systems, important challenges and future research directions are finally specified.

items.title: CNN on ‘Top’: In search of scalable and lightweight image-based jet taggers
items.abstract: Abstract While Transformer-based and standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have proven to be the best performers in classifying different types of jets, they require substantial computational power. We explore the scope of using a lightweight and scalable version of EfficientNet architecture, along with global features of the jet. The end product is computationally inexpensive but is capable of competitive performance. We showcase the efficacy of our network in tagging top-quark jets in a sea of other light quark and gluon jets. The work also sheds light on the importance of global features for both the accuracy and the apparent redundancy of the network’s complexity.

items.title: Beyond PCIe Thrashing and Recursive Sandboxes: High-Throughput 30B Sparse MoE Inference and Symbolic-Gated Hallucination Verification on 4 GB VRAM Workstations
items.abstract: Deploying frontier-scale Large Language Models (LLMs) in the 30-billion-parameter class locally on standard enterprise workstations—typically equipped with 32 GB of host DRAM and an entry-level 4 GB VRAM discrete GPU—presents severe memory capacity and interconnect bandwidth bottlenecks. Existing consumer offloading frameworks rely on dynamic runtime migration of Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) weights across the PCIe bus or multi-turn recursive code-execution sandboxes for factual verification, both of which incur prohibitive latency on 4 GB GPUs and introduce security risks in enterprise environments. In this paper, we present an end-to-end heterogeneous inference and neuro-symbolic verification architecture evaluated on a standard enterprise workstation (Intel Core i7-12700K, 32 GB DRAM, NVIDIA T1000 4 GB VRAM) running a 30.5B-parameter sparse MoE model (Qwen3-30B-A3B). First, we demonstrate empirically that dynamic GPU LRU expert caching degrades token generation throughput by 54.1% (from 18.68 to 8.57 tokens/s) on a 4 GB GPU due to synchronous PCIe cache-miss thrashing. To eliminate runtime PCIe migration, we propose Static Frequency-Based Tensor Partitioning combined with Selective Top-K Softmax Expert Pruning and Hybrid CPU Performance-Core Pinning. By permanently pinning 100% of dense Shared Attention, Router Gate, and Output Head tensors alongside M = 7 full MoE layers in 4 GB VRAM (3,762 MiB allocated), locking the remaining 41 sparse expert layers in aligned SIMD host RAM on Performance cores, and restricting active routing to the Top-4 experts per layer (~1.5B active parameters/token, capturing >92% router probability mass), we achieve 39.18 tokens/s sustained generation (5.7x speedup over cold baseline) and reduce Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) latency by 147x (from 42,811.7 ms to 290.9 ms) while leaving 20.5 GB of host RAM free. Second, we analyze Regime-Aware Heterogeneous Speculative Decoding using a 386 MB Qwen3-0.6B draft model, demonstrating a 94.8% draft token acceptance rate that accelerates full 8-expert inference by +45.1% (18.68 to 27.11 tokens/s). Finally, as a zero-code-execution alternative to Recursive Language Models (RLM), we introduce a Symbolic-Gated Conditional Neural Critic that audits streamed outputs for numerical fidelity and abstract syntax tree (AST) validity in <2 ms (0.403 ms mean), triggering a low-temperature (tau = 0.10) neural repair pass only when the deterministic Grounding Score falls below 100%.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Neural Networks for Differentially Private Tabular Data Synthesis
items.abstract: In differentially private (DP) tabular data synthesis, the consensus is that statistical models are better than neural network (NN)-based methods. However, we argue that this conclusion is incomplete and overlooks the challenge of densely correlated datasets, where intricate dependencies can overwhelm statistical models. In such complex scenarios, neural networks are more suitable due to their capacity to fit complex distributions by learning directly from samples. Despite this potential, existing NN-based algorithms still suffer from significant limitations. We therefore propose MargNet, incorporating successful algorithmic designs of statistical models into neural networks. MargNet applies an adaptive marginal selection strategy and trains the neural networks to generate data that conforms to the selected marginals. On sparsely correlated datasets, our approach achieves utility close to the best statistical method while offering an average 7$\times$ speedup over it. More importantly, on densely correlated datasets, MargNet establishes a new state-of-the-art, reducing fidelity error by up to 26\% compared to the previous best. We release our code on GitHub.\footnote{https://github.com/KaiChen9909/margnet}
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
items.abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

items.title: Area–power–delay Optimized RTL-To-GDSII VLSI Implementation of 16-Bit Ve-Dic Multiplier Using High-Speed Adders
items.abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis and an ASIC-oriented design of a 16-bit Vedic Multiplier based on the Urdhva-Tiryakbhyam algorithm using Kogge-Stone (KSA), Carry Look-Ahead (CLA), and Carry Save (CSA) adders. The architectures are implemented in Verilog HDL and evaluated across 45 nm, 90 nm, and 180 nm technology nodes using the Cadence suite. Pre-layout synthesis metrics (cell count, delay, and power) are analyzed to study performance trade-offs across nodes. Furthermore, physical design placement and routing at 90 nm confirms ASIC standard-cell feasibility, although detailed post-route parasitic extraction is reserved for future hardware prototyping. Comparisons with FPGA-based works demonstrate significant improvements in speed and power efficiency, making the proposed KSA-based design highly suitable for high-speed, low-power VLSI and DSP applications.

items.title: A flexible language model-assisted electronic design automation framework
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) are transforming electronic design automation (EDA) by enhancing design stages such as schematic design, simulation, netlist synthesis, and place-and-route. Existing methods primarily focus these optimisations within isolated open-source EDA tools and often lack the flexibility to handle multiple domains, such as analogue, digital, and radio-frequency design. In contrast, modern systems require to interface with commercial EDA environments, adhere to tool-specific operation rules, and incorporate feedback from design outcomes while supporting diverse design flows. We propose a versatile framework that uses LLMs to generate files compatible with commercial EDA tools and optimise designs using power-performance-area reports. This is accomplished by guiding the LLMs with tool constraints and feedback from design outputs to meet tool requirements and user specifications. The framework is used to evaluate case studies on operational transconductance amplifiers, microstrip patch antennas, and FPGA circuits.

items.title: A Survey on LLMs from a Human-Centric Perspective
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of large language models (LLMs) has positioned them as powerful computational instruments for human-centered research and applications, spanning tasks involving cognition, decision-making, and social interaction. This survey examines LLMs from a human-centric perspective organized around individual and collective levels. We first review LLM competencies across perception, analysis, integration, execution, and social interaction, highlighting both their demonstrated capabilities and the evaluation conditions under which these capabilities are observed. We then explore how LLMs are used across behavioral science, psychology, linguistics, political science, economics, and sociology as research tools, behavioral simulators, and objects of inquiry, covering both individual behavior and collective social processes. Finally, we identify challenges and future research directions, such as improving LLM adaptability, affective-to-behavior evaluation, and cultural sensitivity, while addressing inherent biases and enhancing frameworks for human-AI collaboration. This survey aims to provide a foundational understanding of LLMs from a human-centric perspective, offering insights into their current capabilities and potential for future development.

items.title: A Compact Low Power CCII-Based LIF Neuron with Memristive Synapse Exhibiting Synaptic Plasticity
items.abstract: Biological neural systems perform information processing through the collective operation of neurons and synapses, in which learning is achieved by activity-dependent modification of synaptic strength. Emulating these mechanisms in electronic circuits requires compact, low-power, and scalable implementations of spiking neurons and adaptive synapses. This paper presents a compact, low-power second-generation current conveyor (CCII)- based leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neuron with a memristive synapse exhibiting synaptic plasticity. The proposed neuron operates in the current domain. It employs a CCII to implement weighted summation of presynaptic inputs, leaky membrane integration, and threshold-based spike generation using a low-power comparator and a PMOS-based reset mechanism. Both a resistor and a memristor are used to represent synaptic weights at the neuron inputs. At the same time, a memristive device is employed as the synapse in the learning model to provide continuously variable, emulated memristive conductance. In addition, spike timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is implemented, in which the relative timing difference between presynaptic and postsynaptic spikes governs the change in synaptic strength. A two-neuron system comprising a presynaptic and a postsynaptic neuron, interconnected via a memristor serving as the synapse, is used to demonstrate long-term potentiation (LTP) and long-term depression (LTD). During LTP, the memristor conductance increases, whereas during LTD, the conductance decreases, thereby demonstrating synaptic plasticity similar to biological systems. The proposed circuit is designed and simulated in Cadence Virtuoso using 0.18μm CMOS technology to verify its operational performance. Simulation results validate correct LIF operation, stable learning behaviour, and low power consumption (23 μW) in standard 0.18 μm CMOS technology, confirming the suitability of the proposed neuron-synapse architecture for neuromorphic computing systems.
items.venue: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers

items.title: (A)iSpy: Parasitic Trojans for Machine Learning Infrastructure
items.abstract: Modern machine learning (ML) pipelines depend heavily on third party libraries for graph compilation and hardware acceleration. While current practices audit data and model artifacts or rely on file integrity checks, the execution environment remains implicitly trusted. This blind spot enables active threats where a malicious runtime module interacts directly with live training and inference dynamics: exploiting this interaction allows the Trojan to support complex objectives that are challenging for static code or binary modifications, achieving manipulations impossible for standard data and model level attacks. We expose this vulnerability by presenting AiSPY, a parasitic infrastructure Trojan that subverts MLsystems through an active observe and execute paradigm. Operating within the computation graph, AiSPY monitors transient tensor states to perform targeted, stealthy manipulations with negligible overhead. To violate confidentiality, the Trojan identifies all critical training hyperparameters and covertly exfiltrates them via model weights or output logits. To break integrity, it acts as a gradient amplifier: by observing steganographic triggers, it transforms other- wise weak data poisoning into effective backdoor attacks, increasing success rates from near zero to 100%. We further demonstrate broad extensibility across the machine learning lifecycle by validating auxiliary attacks in the appendix, including subpopulation label flipping, availability disruptions, and inference stage manipulations. Importantly, the evaluated malware scanners do not flag AiSPY because current public rule sets lack coverage for ML runtime Trojans, while the associated poisoned inputs and resulting compromised models bypass state-of-the-art inspection tools. We demonstrate the practicality of this threat with an implementation in the ONNX Runtime training and inference engines.
items.venue: ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS)

items.title: Starscream: Reimagining LLM Sharding on AMD Instinct GPUs with GPU Partitioning
items.abstract: As GPU accelerators grow larger to meet rising compute demands, they exhibit increasingly pronounced non-uniform memory access (NUMA) characteristics that challenge existing LLM frameworks. Chiplet-based architectures provide a practical path to larger GPUs while mitigating manufacturing yield constraints. Modern GPUs such as AMD Instinct MI300X employs such a multi-die design, and further offer GPU partitioning capabilities, partitioning a single physical GPU into multiple logical devices with NUMA-aware memory domains, promising faster kernel launches, and reduced memory access latencies with improved locality. However, current parallelization strategies, designed for homogeneous GPU topologies, when applied under partitioning, extend its unidimensional sharding causing significant performance degradation. Three bottlenecks emerge: (1) memory redundancy; (2) arithmetic intensity collapse; (3) communication overhead from flat collectives. We present Starscream, a rethinking of LLM sharding for the chiplet era. Rather than stretching inter-GPU sharding thinner, Starscream adds intra-GPU sharding along an orthogonal dimension, grounded in three foundational principles: kernel shape preservation, memory redundancy elimination, and communication overhead minimization. These principles form the basis for extending any sharding strategy into the partitioning regime. We demonstrate their effectiveness using tensor parallelism as a case study. On AMD MI300X and MI355X, exploiting partitioning capabilities yields up to 4x speedup for attention and 1.43x for fused GEMMs compared to chiplet-oblivious baselines, demonstrating the effectiveness of chiplet-aware designs. Starscream's principles generalize across sharding strategies and future architectures.

items.title: HARE: Fast Read Disturbance Threshold Profiling in Modern DRAM Chips via Reduced Timing Constraints
items.abstract: Modern DRAM chips are vulnerable to read disturbance, which manifests as bitflips in a victim row physically near an aggressor row that is repeatedly activated. State-of-the-art mitigations rely on accurate and exhaustive profiling of the read disturbance threshold (RDT), i.e., the minimum number of aggressor row activations needed to induce the first bitflip. However, RDT changes significantly and unpredictably over time, motivating online profilers that dynamically adjust a mitigation's RDT configuration. RDT profiling is costly for online profilers (e.g., hundreds of seconds for a 16-bank DDR4 module) because 1) measuring a single DRAM row's RDT requires many activations and 2) each DRAM row can have a different RDT, requiring many rows to be profiled. We introduce HARE, an online RDT profiling technique that intentionally exacerbates read disturbance to quickly profile a DRAM module. HARE's key idea is to reduce the timing constraints between consecutive DRAM commands during profiling. Doing so significantly reduces profiling time by 1) directly reducing the execution time of the profiling command sequence and 2) exacerbating read disturbance such that the first bitflip occurs at a smaller activation count than with the conventional RowHammer sequence. From our characterization of 180 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major DRAM manufacturers, we make three observations. First, HARE measures a DRAM row's RDT 31.2% faster than the RowHammer profiler and a DRAM module's minimum RDT with an average reduction of 21.7%. Second, HARE flips more than 95% of the cells that the RowHammer pattern flips. Third, HARE preserves the RDT ranking of rows well enough such that it can exhaustively reprofile a small set of rows to improve its minimum RDT estimation. Our end-to-end evaluations show that HARE enables significant system performance improvements and outperforms the RowHammer profiler.

items.title: Nonlocal multipolar spin accumulation in altermagnets beyond d-wave
items.abstract: In spin-conserving models of $g$- and $i$-wave altermagnets, the uniform longitudinal conductivity has no spin-odd component. A point injector reveals higher moments of the Fermi velocity through the nonlocal spin accumulation. Boltzmann theory predicts that the rank $m=2,4,6$ of the first nonzero spin-odd velocity moment sets the leading angular harmonic, its asymptotic radial dependence $r^{2-m}$, and its amplitude scaling $τ^{m-3}$ at fixed distance and injected current. For $g$-wave order, the fourth moment produces a fourth angular harmonic with an asymptotic $r^{-2}$ tail. Quantum transport simulations support the radial profiles predicted by finite-geometry Boltzmann theory without an amplitude fit. Across the three symmetries, the quantum amplitudes exceed the Boltzmann predictions based on the Born scattering time by $15-65$\% in the windows analyzed. In a two-contact ribbon, we detect the $g$-wave fourth harmonic at $6.8\,σ$ in an independent set of 1800 disorder realizations using a preselected radial window. Its amplitude decreases when the altermagnetic splitting is reduced.

items.title: 国产AI算力硬件开源技术手册(V1.0)
items.abstract: 摘要 当前全球AI算力发展受限于芯片热密度、存储带宽、芯粒集成、集群互联四大物理工程瓶颈,海外算力生态形成较强的技术与产业链壁垒。国内芯片、存储、封装、高速互联各领域已经积累大量成熟技术基础,但各主体技术分散,缺少一套统一的顶层工程方案完成体系整合。本手册立足于现有国产产业底座,提出一套开放共享的硬件优化技术框架,分别从芯片热管理、存储同步架构、大规模芯粒集成封装、集群高速场互联四个模块给出设计思路、适配方案、预期技术指标与开源交付内容,提出国内多方产业主体协同合作体的组织模式与分工路径。本手册不绑定特定基础物理概念,只输出可用于工程研讨、原型验证的实施方案,旨在助力国内大模型训练硬件支撑体系建设,推动算力硬件技术自主迭代。 Abstract The development of global AI computing power is currently restricted by four major physical and engineering bottlenecks: chip thermal density, memory bandwidth, chiplet integration, and cluster interconnection. Overseas computing ecosystems have formed strong technical and industrial chain barriers. Although China has accumulated mature technologies in chips, storage, advanced packaging, and high-speed interconnection, technical resources are scattered among different enterprises and lack a unified top-level engineering system for integration. Based on the existing domestic industrial foundation, this manual proposes an open hardware optimization framework covering chip thermal management, memory synchronization architecture, large-scale chiplet integration packaging, and high-speed cluster field interconnection. It provides design principles, domestic adaptation schemes, expected technical indicators, and open-source deliverables, and establishes a collaborative mechanism for domestic industrial participants. Without relying on specific basic physical theories, this manual offers implementable engineering solutions and prototype verification directions, aiming to support the construction of domestic large-model training hardware systems and promote independent iteration of domestic AI computing infrastructure.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: ZnO–Te Anti-Ambipolar Switch Integration with Complementary Field-Effect Transistors Enabling a Pull-Middle Architecture for Standard Ternary Inverters
items.abstract: Abstract We demonstrate a pull-middle architecture for standard ternary inverters (STIs) operating at 77 K, enabled by the cointegration of a ZnO–Te antiambipolar switch (AAS) and vertically stacked ZnO/Te complementary field-effect transistors (CFETs) using a BEOL-compatible low-temperature process (≤150 °C). Operation at 77 K not only isolates the intrinsic pull-middle switching mechanism by suppressing thermally activated off-currents but also establishes the architecture’s immediate viability for extreme-environment computing, such as radiation-hardened space data centers and cryogenic aerospace systems. In this architecture, the ZnO–Te AAS acts as an independent pull-middle device connected to an explicit Vdd/2 node, while the ZnO and Te FETs in the CFET serve as the pull-down and pull-up devices, respectively. Unlike conventional ternary logic schemes governed by precise pull-up/pull-down current matching, by explicitly clamping the intermediate state, this architecture structurally prevents variation-induced voltage shifts and suppresses static power dissipation. Consequently, the proposed STI exhibits a narrow middle-state voltage distribution across 25 cells and achieves an I/O swing ratio of 1, with cascaded operation without level-restoring circuitry supported by measurement-calibrated circuit simulations. Ultimately, this vertically integrated ZnO/Te STI offers a compact and variation-tolerant platform for cryogenic logic, while presenting a material-optimization pathway toward room-temperature multivalued systems.

items.title: Transferable Machine Learning of Electronic Hamiltonians with Superposition-of-Atomic-Potentials Features
items.abstract: Abstract Machine learning of electronic Hamiltonians offers a unified route to electronic wave functions and physical observables. We introduce a Hamiltonian learning framework built on electronic features derived from the superposition-of-atomic-potentials (SAP) approximation, an efficient self-consistent-field initial guess that captures essential electron–electron screening. SAP quantities define a symmetry-adapted intrinsic atomic orbital learning basis and provide physics-informed inputs to an orbital-based graph neural network that predicts converged Kohn–Sham Fock matrices. To extend the approach to larger basis sets, we further develop a downfolding scheme that predicts large-basis electronic structure from minimal-basis features. On the QM9 data set, the model accurately reproduces frontier and core orbital energies, dipole moments, and the full density of states. For organic charge-transport materials, it yields accurate intermolecular transfer integrals for benzene, tetracyanoquinodimethane (TCNQ), and tetrathiafulvalene (TTF) dimers. The model also generalizes to unseen substituted-benzene heterodimers, with a mean absolute error of 4.8 meV. These results establish SAP-based Hamiltonian learning as a transferable and scalable tool for high-throughput electronic-structure prediction.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Thermal annealing effects on total-ionizing-dose radiation hardness in HfO2 /SiC MOS structures
items.abstract: Abstract Thermal annealing is a critical step in fabricating hafnium oxide/silicon carbide (HfO 2 /SiC) metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) devices. However, its effect on total ionizing dose (TID) radiation hardness remains unclear. We find that for the unannealed Sample A, γ -ray irradiation (300 krad(Si)) produces a positive flat-band voltage shift (V fb ) of 1.76 V. Compared with Sample A, the annealed Sample B (975 ℃ rapid thermal annealing, RTA) shows a reduction in the interface trap density ( D it ) at the HfO 2 /SiC interface from 1.01 × 10 13 cm -2 ·eV -1 to 3.67 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 , and an increase in the breakdown field strength of the MOS capacitor from 5.28 MV/cm to 6.91 MV/cm. However, Sample B suffers from adverse effects after irradiation, such as a negative V fb shift, a reduction in barrier height ( φ b ), and a degradation of the breakdown field (1.98 MV/cm). Therefore, we propose a pre-annealing step at 550 ℃ for 30 minutes (Sample C) prior to the RTA. This pre-annealing converts the negative V fb shift caused by TID effects into a positive V fb shift. Furthermore, the D it of this sample drops to 1.61 × 10 12 cm -2 ·eV -1 after irradiation, while φ b increases from 0.42 eV to 1.18 eV. XPS depth profiling reveals irradiation-induced redistribution of Hf-O coordination and the emergence of an O-Hf-C interfacial component, which we interpret as consistent with oxygen-mediated defect reordering. These findings reveal how thermal annealing influences the TID radiation response of HfO 2 dielectrics and provide critical guidance for the development of radiation-tolerant HfO 2 /SiC devices intended for extreme-environment applications.

items.title: The Singularity is 4 Bits: Compiling Bounded Specialist Chains for Local Neuromorphic Execution
items.abstract: Many decisions recur, and when their inputs, state and allowed outcomes can be written down, they do not need a general-purpose model on every call. Borrowing the form of "Attention Is All You Need," this paper proposes that for recurring bounded decisions, meaning decisions with fixed, fully specified inputs and outcomes, one compiled specialist whose stored synaptic weights are four bits is enough. We built an architecture that compiles each such task into a small specialist that runs locally, and links specialists into chains by passing explicit, typed state from one to the next. The compiler derives relational features, such as whether two fields are equal, from the declared types of the task's fields. It then trains a small linear classifier, converts its scores into four-bit synaptic weights, and saves the model with the rules for mapping inputs, reading outputs and ending execution. Only the stored synaptic weight is four bits. Accumulation and host arithmetic use wider integers. Executed in the official simulator of BrainChip's Akida software development kit, the saved four-bit specialists made no errors on 75, 55 and 60 repeated withheld decisions across three finite tasks defined by written rules, each run from five fresh random starting points (initializations), and completed all 15 multi-step trajectories. On a circular-dial task, an ordered relation made no errors on 60 withheld decisions. Equality-only features made 45 errors and raw fields made 59. An exact-arithmetic certificate proves that no linear classifier on either of those two feature sets can strictly separate the training labels. Each saved specialist is a 78,054-byte file, and a chain experiment preserves the capacity-gate trajectory across one, two, four and twelve virtual target placements. Four bits is thus a precision shown to work for compiling recurring decisions into bounded, locally executed specialists. Next come physical execution on a twelve-chip Akida board, larger task suites and chains that span devices.
