items.title: SynthStrategy: Extracting and Formalizing Latent Strategic Insights from LLMs in Organic Chemistry
items.abstract: Abstract Modern computer-assisted synthesis planning (CASP) systems show promise at generating chemically valid reaction steps but struggle to incorporate strategic considerations such as convergent assembly, protecting-group minimization, and optimal ring-forming sequences. We introduce a methodology that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to distill synthetic knowledge into code. Our system analyzes synthesis routes and translates strategic principles into executable Python functions representing diverse strategic and tactical rules, such as strategic functional group interconversions, protecting strategies and ring construction features. We validate the use of LLM-as-a-judge in this domain, demonstrating their efficacy in evaluating synthesis-specific code generation. By formalizing this knowledge as verifiable code rather than simple heuristics, we create testable, interpretable representations of synthetic strategy. We release the complete codebase and the USPTO-ST data set─synthesis routes annotated with strategic tags. This framework unlocks a novel capability for CASP: natural language-based route retrieval, achieving 74.5% Top-3 accuracy on our benchmark. We further validate our library through temporal analysis of historical trends and chemically intuitive route clustering that offers more granular partitioning than common previous methods. This work bridges the tactical-strategic divide in CASP, enabling specification, search, and evaluation of routes by strategic criteria rather than structure alone.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

items.title: Synergistic Effect of Hybrid Polarized Spin Currents Enables Sub-Nanosecond and Energy-Efficient Field-Free Switching on a Wafer-Scale Platform
items.abstract: Spin-orbit torque magnetoresistive random access memory (SOT-MRAM) exhibits intrinsic potential for next-generation magnetic memory, whereas robust wafer-level field-free switching (FFS) of nanosized perpendicular magnetic tunnel junctions (pMTJ) remains a critical challenge for practical applications. Here, we present a robust FFS of 90 nm pMTJs on 300 mm wafers driven by the synergistic effect of y- and z-polarized spin currents generated at the antiferromagnetic (AFM)/nonmagnetic (NM) interface. Experimental results demonstrate that an appropriate combination of both y- and z-spin polarizations is able to significantly improve the FFS performance. 90 nm pMTJ arrays are fabricated on 300 mm wafers, where a mean tunnel magnetoresistance ratio (TMR) of 140%, an endurance of exceeding 1012 cycles, and a robust field-free SOT switching at sub-nanosecond (down to 0.2 ns) are simultaneously achieved. Robust FFS is observed at temperature up to 100 °C, and the switching polarity remains unchanged after 1T magnetic field disturbance. With the assistance of the voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effect, the switching current density is reduced by 20% and the switching energy can be as low as 0.35 pJ/bit. This work paves the way for SOT-MRAM toward commercialization.

items.title: Study planning is better served by Monte Carlo simulation than AI-generated participants
items.abstract: ‘Silicon samples’, AI-generated synthetic data based on demographic profiles, have been proposed to help plan research. Here, I argue that Monte Carlo simulation already does this job transparently, and that generative AI is better used to help write such simulations.

items.title: Structural and electronic properties of oxygen deficient HfO2-x thin films: from insulator to metal
items.abstract: Abstract Hafnium oxide (HfO₂) and its oxygen-deficient variants (HfO₂₋ₓ) are key candidates for next-generation electronics, ranging from photonics and photocatalysis to both resistive and ferroelectric memories. Sub-stoichiometric HfO₂₋ₓ reduces the forming voltage in ReRAM devices and stabilizes the orthorhombic ferroelectric phase crucial for non-volatile FeRAM, yet a systematic understanding of its electronic evolution remains elusive. Here, we synthesize a complete series of HfO₂₋ₓ thin films spanning from stoichiometric oxide to pure metal and map their structural and electronic transformations. By combining X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction, resistivity profiling, and Hf L₃-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure, we reveal clear stoichiometry-driven trends in bonding, phase formation, and electronic structure, providing a definitive reference for tailoring HfO₂₋ₓ in advanced memory and photonic applications.

items.title: Single-Tube Eight-Plex Full-Length PCR-NGS for High-Resolution HLA Typing: Assay Validation and Exploratory ADO-Risk Quality Control
items.abstract: Background: High-resolution typing of human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genes is a core technology for dissecting genetic polymorphism in the MHC region of the human genome and has important clinical value in hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, solid organ transplantation, and tumor immunotherapy. Although full-length HLA typing methods based on next-generation sequencing (NGS) can achieve high-resolution results, long-range PCR amplification carries the risk of allelic dropout (ADO). Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in primer-binding regions may cause the amplification failure of a given allele, leading to heterozygotes being misclassified as homozygotes and resulting in HLA typing errors. Such mistyping during donor selection for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may lead to HLA matching errors between donors and recipients, increasing the risk of graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) or transplant rejection. Existing NGS approaches generally rely on a single set of amplification primers and lack an independent verification mechanism. Methods: This study designed a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay and performed systematic methodological validation. The assay simultaneously co-amplifies eight classical HLA genes (HLA-A, -B, -C, -DRB1, -DQB1, -DPB1, -DPA1, and -DQA1) in a single tube, with primers anchored in the conserved 5′UTR and 3′UTR regions to capture the complete gene sequences, and high-resolution typing was performed using the HLA-HD software. Sanger sequencing-based typing (SBT) and PacBio/ONT third-generation long-read sequencing served as dual gold standards, and multi-level validation was completed using 92 anonymous peripheral blood genomic DNA samples from the Chinese population and the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line. During primer testing, we found that two samples exhibited allele loss at the HLA-DRB1 locus in the context of SNPs in the primer-binding region, indicating that ADO risk exists in practice; after adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, ADO in these samples was resolved, but the limitations of PCR technology and the high polymorphism of HLA dictate that ADO cannot be fundamentally eliminated by primer adjustment. Accordingly, we further designed, in an exploratory manner, a 6-plex QC assay whose primer-binding regions do not overlap at all with those of the 8-plex system, for proportional spot-checking verification in large-scale sample testing. Typing results were reported and used for consistency statistics primarily at 3-field resolution; the assay can read up to 4-field resolution, but given that the accuracy of 4-field interpretation cannot be independently verified by existing gold standards, 4-field data were retained only as exploratory supplementary results. Results: (1)Validation of the 8-plex system: For the 10 SBT reference samples, the 2-field typing concordance rate was 100%, and 4-field high-resolution results could be output; the 8-plex typing of 10 blinded samples matched the PacBio third-generation sequencing 3-field results 100%; the MDA-MB-231 standard cell line typing showed no discrepancies compared with the official Cellosaurus data. (2) Discovery of ADO risk: During primer testing, two samples that were heterozygous by SBT were misclassified as homozygous by the 8-plex assay; sequence alignment analysis revealed high-frequency SNPs in the primer-binding region of the 8-plex assay for these two samples, suggesting that primer binding may have been affected. After adjusting the primers to more conserved positions, the 8-plex typing results were consistent with SBT, confirming heterozygosity. (3) Exploration of 6-plex QC: Stratified validation included 31 samples in total, comprising 10 samples dually validated by the 8-plex assay and third-generation sequencing, one standard cell line, and 20 randomly sampled clinical samples; the 8-plex and 6-plex typing results were completely consistent for all these samples; the allele depth ratio (ADR) was mostly ≤2.0 across loci in the 6-plex assay. (4) Performance evaluation: The ADR was mostly ≤2.0 across all samples; the ranking of polymorphism abundance at each locus was consistent with the trends in published Chinese population cohorts; the rare allele HLA-DPB1*744:01 was successfully captured and verified by third-generation sequencing (ONT). Conclusions: This study designed and validated a single-tube 8-plex full-length PCR-NGS HLA typing assay, which showed stable amplification, accurate typing, strong rare-allele capture capability, short turnaround time, and controllable batch testing costs in 92 Chinese population samples. During validation, ADO risk was found to exist in practice; adjusting primers for known SNP sites can correct specific ADO events but cannot fundamentally eliminate the risk. The 6-plex independent QC assay designed on this basis showed complete concordance with the 8-plex results in 31 samples, but its ability to correct real ADO events remains a theoretical inference and an indirect validation, and further evaluation through long-term clinical accumulation or large-scale parallel validation is still needed. This method is expected to provide an accurate, economical, and practical new approach for clinical high-resolution HLA typing.

items.title: Simultaneous extraction of multiple buffer-trap parameters in GaN HEMTs via measurement-window sweeping: A TCAD study
items.abstract: Abstract The duration of the measurement window strongly affects the observed current collapse in GaN HEMTs and can obscure the individual contributions of buffer traps. Using TCAD simulations of output measurements following off-state stress, this work tracks trap emission and recapture and develops a multi-exponential time-domain deconvolution method based on measurement-window sweeping. The drain current sampled at the knee voltage is analyzed as a function of the measurement-window duration to extract characteristic time constants and recovery-current amplitudes. Two-trap tests resolve the distinct recovery steps associated with Fe and deeper trap components and quantify their individual contributions. For multi-component responses, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) and time-constant-collapse criteria are used jointly to determine the number of resolvable components and identify overfitting. In the uniform-profile multi-trap test, the fitted time constants of the dominant recovery components agree with the prescribed values within approximately 16%. A further test with a nonuniform Fe profile resolves distinct fast E1 and slow Fe recovery components, with time-constant deviations of −0.85% and −29.3%, respectively. By simultaneously extracting characteristic time constants and relative contributions to the recoverable current-collapse amplitude, the method provides a quantitative basis for assessing the impact of individual trap components and guiding epitaxial and process optimization.

items.title: Self-Specializing Neuromorphic Computer: A Distributed Architecture Beyond the NPU
items.abstract: A concept paper proposing a self-specialising neuromorphic compute architecture built from existing technologies. Core ideas: Hardware that specialises itself through use: a RISC core offloading work to reconfigurable logic and analog memristor crossbars. Task training: specialisation through exposure to a varied class of related tasks, with checkpoints for rollback. Routing learned from results: inter-cell routes weighted by accuracy, speed and round-trip time, giving self-organisation and self-healing. Includes the motivation for departing from digital simulation of neural networks, related work, one illustrative implementation (component budget and power targets), and open questions for the community. Shared to stimulate discussion rather than as a finished design. Feedback welcome.

items.title: Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: replication package (code, results and paper)
items.abstract: Code, result tables, figures, decision and assumption logs, and the working paper for Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree. An open panel of 24,210 listing-months of posted GPU rental prices (NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026), four identification strategies for the age-price profile, asset values and economic life, and a seven-firm earnings restatement. `make all` rebuilds every table, figure and the paper from the archived raw files. The raw files whose sources permit redistribution and the public panel are deposited as a separate Zenodo dataset; the rest are re-fetched by the repository's collectors, with checksums in release/raw_manifest.csv. Code is MIT-licensed; the dataset is CC BY 4.0. See README.md.

items.title: Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: GPU rental-price panel and redistributable raw data
items.abstract: Data deposit for the working paper Rental-Implied Depreciation of AI Accelerators: Why the Estimates Disagree (Ajai Upadhyaya, November 2026). release/dataset/gpu_rental_panel.csv is the public panel of monthly median posted GPU rental prices (USD per GPU-hour, nominal and in 2025 dollars) for NVIDIA V100 to B200, 2017-2026; rows available only from the SkyPilot catalog history, which has no licence, are omitted. data/raw/ holds every raw file whose source permits redistribution: the author's own GPU benchmark runs and hand-recorded prices, Epoch AI hardware data (CC BY 4.0), EIA Form 861M, BLS CPI-U and SEC EDGAR filings and XBRL facts, each with a sidecar recording source URL, retrieval time and HTTP status. release/raw_manifest.csv lists every raw file used by the paper with its SHA-256 and the command that re-fetches the files not deposited here. Code, results and the paper are in the companion software record, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24143074. The panel is CC BY 4.0; third-party files keep their sources' terms.

items.title: Raman Thermometry for Thermal Transport: Principles, Progress and Prospects Across Low‐Dimensional Materials and Devices
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Raman thermometry is widely used to determine thermal‐transport properties from atomically thin membranes to active device regions. Raman‐active phonon modes change predictably with temperature, enabling a focused laser to act as both heater and thermometer. Measurements of the power‐, position‐ or frequency‐dependent Raman response, interpreted with an appropriate heat‐transfer model, can provide in‐plane thermal conductivity and, in selected geometries, interfacial thermal conductance without electrical contacts. Since the first optothermal measurement of suspended monolayer graphene in 2008, the method has been applied to graphene and related carbon materials, transition‐metal dichalcogenides, hexagonal boron nitride, semiconductor nanowires, wide‐bandgap devices and thermoelectric films. Two‐laser, frequency‐domain, transient, Stokes/anti‐Stokes and scanning implementations have extended the technique to supported and device‐integrated specimens. This review examines the physical basis, experimental configurations, heat‐transfer models, results for representative materials and main sources of uncertainty. Particular attention is given to absorptance, beam size, substrate heat leakage, thermomechanical stress and nonequilibrium phonon populations. We conclude with practical guidance on method selection, model validity and uncertainty reporting.

items.title: Negative differential transconductance in deterministically transferred CVD-Grown monolayer WSe2/MoS2 heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Electrostatic control of the band alignment in two-dimensional van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures is a fundamental requirement for realizing low-power tunnelling electronics, multi-valued logic and next-generation functional devices. Yet, its experimental demonstration in scalable chemical vapour deposition (CVD)-grown heterostructures remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate a simple heterostructure field-effect transistor based on deterministically transferred CVD-grown monolayers of WSe2 and MoS2. These materials are stacked using a contact-first, transfer-later fabrication strategy that enables localized electrostatic modulation of the heterointerface. The fabricated device exhibits two distinct drain-current minima in its transfer characteristics, with the first minimum occurring at a fixed back-gate voltage, while the second minimum shifts with drain voltage. Analysis around the first current minimum reveals a pronounced negative differential transconductance (NDT), with a peak-to-valley current ratio (PVCR) of 16 at room temperature, providing a clear electrical signature of band-to-band tunnelling (BTBT). The observed transport behaviour originates from strong electrostatic doping induced by the back gate, which drives the WSe2/MoS2 heterointerface from a staggered (type-II) to a broken (type-III) bandgap alignment, enabling interlayer BTBT under large negative gate bias. As the gate voltage is increased, the loss of the broken-gap alignment terminates the tunnelling process, producing a gate-voltage-pinned current minimum and the associated NDT response. These findings establish that CVD-grown vdW heterostructures can achieve controllable electrostatic band engineering and room-temperature tunnelling phenomena using a simple single-back-gate architecture, providing an experimentally practical pathway towards future low-power tunnelling transistors, multi-valued logic circuits, and electrically reconfigurable two-dimensional electronic devices.
authors: O V Vishnu Vardhan Koundinya Koundinya

items.title: Multiscale ensemble Monte Carlo of transport and gas sensing in monolayer MoS 2
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional semiconductors, such as monolayer MoS 2 , combine a technologically useful band gap with a thickness of three atomic planes. The entire carrier density then lies within a few Å of the surface, which makes them useful as field-effect-transistor channels and as chemically sensitive devices. Device design for MoS 2 needs a transport model whose scattering rates are computed rather than calibrated, whose predictions are tested against experiment, and that spans the scales from electron-phonon coupling to terminal current and sensor response. We present a self-consistent ensemble Monte Carlo (EMC) framework for monolayer MoS 2 built on the ViennaEMC solver, which couples a Boltzmann transport model to Poisson's equation with degenerate free-carrier statistics. The transport model carries wavevector-dependent acoustic, polar-optical, homopolar and intervalley phonon scattering within and between the K valleys and the spin-orbit-split Q valleys, together with remote substrate phonons, screened charged impurities and surface roughness. Every intrinsic input of the transport model is computed from first principles for this work, namely the band structure of the K and Q valleys, the phonon energies, sound velocities and dielectric response, and the electron-phonon couplings from density-functional perturbation theory (DFPT) matrix elements at 34 explicit phonon wavevectors and from Wannier interpolation with the two-dimensional long-range treatment. The model therefore contains no fitted transport parameter and no coupling taken from another calculation, and its scattering rates are checked against an independent solution of the linearised Boltzmann equation with the same couplings. The EMC velocity-field characteristic feeds a one-dimensional channel model, which is verified against a direct self-consistent three-dimensional EMC simulation of the gated channel and reproduces the measured transfer characteristics of a CVD monolayer device in air and vacuum. An ambient/adsorbate extension reproduces the measured conductivity response to oxygen partial pressure and the concentration dependence of NO 2 and NH 3 sensing of independent monolayer devices.

items.title: Multifunctional vortex magnetic tunnel junctions with optical and radio-frequency inputs for neuromorphic computing
items.abstract: Abstract The brain co-locates memory and processing, but many neuromorphic devices need standby power or separate memory from nonlinear computation. Here we show that vortex magnetic tunnel junctions with a non-volatile, thermally programmable storage layer provide two complementary nonlinear channels in one nanopillar. The laser-induced voltage is linear in laser power but cubic in direct-current bias, making the bias current a nonlinear, programmable weight, whereas radio-frequency excitation is rectified into a frequency-dependent voltage. Crossbar simulations using measured responses classify handwritten digits with 95.4\% accuracy using optical inputs and 94.9\% using radio-frequency inputs, comparable to an equal-size digital single-layer network. Microlenses focusing light to sub-micrometre spots, one formed directly on a junction, and a flip-chip-mounted vertical-cavity surface-emitting laser array provide a route to on-chip optical addressing. Operating both channels together could combine optical and radio-frequency inputs within one nanoscale device, making vortex junctions reprogrammable multi-input building blocks for analog neuromorphic hardware.

items.title: Multidimensional Bayesian Optimization of Nanosheet Double-Gate LDMOS for Enhanced Power Figure of Merit
items.abstract: Abstract This work investigates and optimizes a nanosheet-inspired Double-Gate Lateral Double-Diffused Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (DG-LDMOS) architecture using Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations combined with Bayesian Optimization (BO), addressing the limitations of sequential manual tuning. By progressively expanding the optimization space from individual parameters to a six-dimensional design space, the optimized nanosheet DG-LDMOS intended for switched-mode operation achieves an intrinsic ultra-low specific on-state resistance of 0.17~m$\Omega\cdot$mm$^{2}$ and a breakdown voltage of 11.32~V, corresponding to a power figure of merit (FOM) of 738~kW/mm$^{2}$. The results reveal that FOM enhancement originates from coupled geometrical and doping optimization, which simultaneously shortens the conduction path, redistributes the lateral electric field, and enhances near-interface carrier transport. These findings demonstrate the importance of simultaneous optimization of strongly coupled device parameters and establish the nanosheet DG-LDMOS as a physics-based foundation for subsequent three-dimensional Gate-All-Around (GAA) LDMOS development.

items.title: Modeling the inner electric double layer using short-range machine learning potentials: A critical assessment
items.abstract: Atomistic simulations of electrochemical interfaces typically require large system sizes and long simulation times to obtain reliable thermodynamic properties. In this context, machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) allow for computationally efficient sampling compared to density functional theory-based molecular dynamics simulations. Although conventional short-range MLIPs are recognized as inadequate for modeling the (potentially nanometer-wide) diffuse layer, they may still be capable of describing the inner electric double layer that is relevant for electrochemical reactions. Here, we evaluate the performance of common (short-ranged) MLIP architectures [the deep potential DP, the (graph) atomic cluster expansion-based models GRACE and MACE, and the pre-trained eSEN-OC25] for charged Au/electrolyte interfaces. In the evaluation, we focus on the effect of message passing and on the potentially adverse effect of data interference when training for a broad range of surface charges. Our results suggest that both local and message-passing models are able to reliably learn the interfacial structure when training on a single charge state. However, when trained on datasets that span multiple charge states, the MLIPs tested yield inconsistent predictions of interfacial water orientation and ion distributions. This behavior can be traced to the MLIPs being "blind" to the actual surface charge. Message-passing models show somewhat greater robustness to mixed-charge training data, likely due to their larger receptive field, but are still prone to artifacts and errors in the description of the interfacial structure. Overall, our results provide practical guidance on the expected accuracy and cross-charge-state transferability of short-ranged MLIPs for the description of the inner layer of electrode/electrolyte interfaces that will be relevant to their use in computational electrocatalysis.

items.title: Low-thermal-budget solution-processed montmorillonite dielectric for low-voltage 2D electronics
items.abstract: Abstract Low-voltage and high-performance electronic devices based on two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors demand high-quality dielectrics with efficient capacitive gating. However, it currently relies on specially engineered atomic layer deposition (ALD) of ultrathin high- k HfO 2 and ZrO 2 , or high-temperature vapor-phase growth of 2D dielectrics with post-growth transfer process. Here, we report a facile solution-processed 2D dielectric with an ultra-low thermal budget (i.e., at room temperature), while delivering competitive device metrics (e.g., low operating voltage and small hysteresis). This is enabled by an organic-free colloidal ink of montmorillonite (MTM) in environmentally friendly water solvent, eliminating the need for organic ligands or surfactants and thus the post-deposition high-temperature thermal annealing. Specifically, all-solution-processed MoS 2 field-effect transistors with MTM dielectric exhibit a low operating voltage of 1 V and small hysteresis (down to 1 mV). The solution process is generally compatible with diverse n-type and p-type 2D semiconductors such as MoS 2 , MoSe 2 and WSe 2 . Moreover, the robust and reproducible MTM dielectric enables scalable device integration into logic circuits, including inverters, AND, NOR, and NAND gates, as well as static random-access memory (SRAM). The scalable room-temperature solution-processed 2D dielectric offers a route to all-solution-processed and low-voltage 2D electronics.

items.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high-κ dielectrics
items.abstract: Abstract Aggressive scaling in silicon electronics—although essential for improving power, performance, area and cost—faces increasing challenges in further reducing power consumption due to electrostatic and leakage constraints 1,2 . Achieving efficient operation at low supply voltages therefore requires new materials and gate-stack engineering strategies. Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductors offer intrinsic advantages because their atomic thickness affords excellent gate control, and their sizable bandgaps suppress off-state current. However, a major obstacle is the imperfect interface between 2D channels and gate dielectrics, which degrades subthreshold swing, hysteresis and bias-temperature instability 3 . Here we demonstrate that a wafer-scale, transferable, single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric can be van der Waals integrated with 2D transition metal dichalcogenides. The obtained pristine 2D-dielectric interface enables subthreshold swing close to the thermal limit, record-low hysteresis and well-matched transfer characteristics for both n- and p-type enhancement-mode field-effect transistors. Building on this, we demonstrate complementary field-effect transistors, whose inverters achieve high voltage gain and large noise margins with subpicowatt static power consumption. These results highlight the promise of 2D semiconductors for ultra-low-power operation.

items.title: LLM-guided adaptive segmentation of tunnel linings from point clouds
items.abstract: Automated inspection of segmental tunnel linings requires adaptive segmentation from 3D point clouds, yet expert-tuned pipelines often degrade when tunnel conditions vary. This paper presents R4Tun, a large language model (LLM)-driven adaptation framework that extends an expert-designed pipeline (SAM4Tun) with bounded parameter tuning informed by structured context: memory ($m$), state ($s$), and knowledge ($k$). Evaluated on 30 selected Seg2Tunnel subsets (13 regular, 17 complex) across three LLMs, the full $m+s+k$ design raised mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) from 0.18 to 0.43--0.48 and overall accuracy (OA) from 0.42 to 0.59--0.65 relative to the static SAM4Tun baseline, with the near-reference regular (staggered) subsets reaching mIoU 0.784--0.796 across LLMs. Across 270 (30 tunnels $\times$ 3 different LLMs $\times$ 3 context settings) runs, the LLMs showed similar parameter-adjustment trends (with overlapping 95\% CIs on mean gains) and consistently adjusted a shared set of critical parameters. These results support R4Tun as a controlled, label-free, cross-LLM adaptation mechanism in the tested SAM4Tun--Seg2Tunnel setting, demonstrating consistent accuracy gains; we position R4Tun as a mechanism contribution rather than a deployable final-inspection system, in which each bounded parameter change is auditable via logged rationales.

items.title: LK-Model-Based TCAD Simulation of Hafnium-Oxide-Based Ferroelectric Memcapacitors for Radiation-Tolerant Neuromorphic Capacitive Synapses
items.abstract: Abstract A W/HZO/HfO2/W/Si ferroelectric memcapacitor was simulated in Silvaco TCAD using the Landau-Khalatnikov (LK) ferroelectric model to examine multilevel capacitance modulation, total ionizing dose (TID) effects, and device-to-system neuromorphic behavior. The simulations show that increasing the write-voltage amplitude strengthens polarization modulation in the HZO layer, producing wider P-V hysteresis loops, clearer switching-current responses, and improved capacitance-state separation. The capacitive memory window (CMW), defined as the zero-bias capacitance-density difference between the upper and lower C-V branches, increases with write voltage, indicating enhanced multilevel capacitance tunability. Under TID irradiation, oxide charge trapping and the associated electric-field perturbation reduce the C-V branch separation and CMW in the adopted model, while distinguishable capacitance states are retained within the investigated dose range. The TCAD-extracted capacitance states were further mapped to synaptic weights for multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based MNIST evaluation. Although irradiation compresses the available capacitance range, the normalized weight states remain sufficiently ordered for stable classification in this simulation framework. These results provide a device-to-system TCAD workflow for evaluating hafnium-based ferroelectric memcapacitors as candidate radiation-tolerant capacitive synapses.

items.title: In-sensor computing paradigms for neuromorphic motion vision
items.abstract: Motion perception is fundamental to autonomous systems and requires the extraction of position, direction, velocity, and acceleration from dynamic visual scenes. Conventional frame-based sensors, silicon event cameras, and position-sensitive detectors provide established solutions, but data transfer and peripheral processing can impose substantial costs in resource-constrained applications. In-sensor computing offers a complementary approach by embedding selected encoding and processing functions in the physical dynamics of optoelectronic devices. This review examines general-purpose motion encoding and task-specific motion processing. Within general-purpose encoding, optoelectronic event motion encoding and fading-memory motion encoding address data redundancy through distinct mechanisms. The former mimics retinal ON/OFF signaling. Programmable bipolar photoresponses provide signals of opposite polarity, while temporal dynamics enable the generation of transient events suitable for processing by spiking neural networks. The latter uses fading-memory devices to retain recent optical inputs as decaying electrical states. When assembled into arrays, these devices act as physical reservoir units that map spatiotemporal inputs into high-dimensional states, from which a trained readout can extract motion information such as trajectories and velocity. For task-specific applications, specialized devices generate collision-sensitive and direction-selective responses at the sensory front end, potentially reducing downstream processing requirements. Finally, we discuss challenges in array uniformity, adaptive operation, peripheral integration, and consistent performance evaluation.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: Implementation of a Speed Optimized Pipelined 32-Bit Floating Point Multiplier for Performance – Critical VLSI Systems
items.abstract: Floating-point multiplication is a critical operation in modern digital systems, including signal processing, scientific computing, graphics processing, and high-performance embedded applications. With increasing computational demands, high-speed and area-efficient arithmetic units are essential. This paper presents the design and VLSI implementation of a 32-bit single-precision float- ing-point multiplier optimized for enhanced performance through architectural improvements. The proposed design improves mantissa multiplication using Ra- dix-4 modified Booth encoding to reduce partial products, thereby lowering switching activity and propagation delay. A Wallace tree reduction structure is employed for fast parallel partial-product compression, significantly accelerating accumulation compared to conventional array multipliers. To further enhance throughput, a pipelined architecture is introduced, dividing computation into bal- anced stages to minimize critical path delay and increase operating frequency. Exponent addition with bias adjustment, along with systematic normalization and rounding units, ensures accurate and stable floating-point computation, including proper handling of edge cases. The design is implemented in Verilog HDL and synthesized using standard VLSI tools. Results demonstrate improved timing performance and optimized hardware utilization compared to conventional archi- tectures, achieving an effective balance between speed, area, and complexity.

items.title: GraphAgents: Knowledge Graph-Guided Agentic AI for Cross-Domain Materials Design
items.abstract: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) promise to accelerate discovery by reasoning across the ever-expanding landscape of scientific knowledge. Yet, as the reservoir of knowledge grows, the challenge is no longer access to information but rather the ability to connect it in meaningful, domain-spanning ways. In materials science, where discoveries and new hypotheses emerge from bridging insights across disciplines and demand the integration of concepts from molecular chemistry to mechanical performance, this challenge is especially acute. Neither human researchers nor single-agent LLMs can contend with this torrent of information, with the latter often producing brittle reasoning and hallucinations. To address this bottleneck, we introduce a multiagent framework guided by large-scale knowledge graphs to address the urgent challenge of finding sustainable substitutes for per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), a class of synthetic chemicals widely used in industrial and consumer applications that are the subject of increasing regulatory scrutiny due to concerns raised in scientific literature and evolving policy efforts to ban certain PFAS compounds. Agents in the framework specialize in problem decomposition, evidence retrieval, design parameter extraction, and graph traversal, uncovering latent connections across distinct pockets of scientific knowledge that support downstream hypothesis generation for PFAS-free materials. Our ablation studies show that the full multiagent pipeline outperforms single-shot prompting, underscoring the value of distributed specialization and relational reasoning. We show that by tailoring graph traversal strategies, the system can alternate between exploitative searches that focus hypothesis generation on domain-critical outcomes and exploratory searches that surface emergent cross-connections in the broader network. Shown through the exemplar of biomedical tubing, the framework generates sustainable material alternatives to PFAS-based tubing that balance tribological performance, thermal stability, chemical resistance, and biocompatibility. This work establishes a framework that combines knowledge graphs with multiagent reasoning to expand the materials design space and reveal interdisciplinary connections. We showcase several initial PFAS-free design candidates to demonstrate the approach.

items.title: Generative AI adoption and scientific output: Quasi-experimental evidence on heterogeneous changes across 26 disciplines
items.abstract: Using monthly OpenAlex data on 92 million publications across 26 academic fields (2015–2025), we examine publication growth associated with large language model (LLM) adoption through a quasi-experimental difference-in-differences design around ChatGPT’s release. The pooled estimate is statistically indistinguishable from zero. However, fields with one standard deviation higher pre-existing AI intensity show 4.52 percentage points greater output growth per percentage point of measured adoption ( 𝑝 = 0 . 0 1 0 ). Expanded keyword definitions reduce this estimate to 1.21–1.75 percentage points. Computer Science shows an estimated cumulative output increase of 8.7% by late 2025. These findings indicate heterogeneous field-level publication responses, with magnitudes sensitive to how adoption is measured.

items.title: Gap‐Filling Stencil Lithography for Precise and High Yield Patterning of Two‐Dimensional Materials
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Two‐dimensional materials (2DMs) are considered revolutionary candidates for manufacturing electronics because of their atomically thin nature and exceptional electrical properties. Lithography is essential for patterning 2DMs and fabricating electronic devices. However, conventional water‐based processes such as photolithography fail to achieve high‐yield production because of 2DM delamination from the substrate. Although non‐water‐based stencil lithography is an alternative, the inherent gap between the mask and substrate causes blurring, obscuring high‐precision definition. In this study, we present gap‐filling stencil lithography (GSL), which introduces a protective layer to eliminate this gap, thereby suppressing blurring and enabling precise patterning for 2DMs. Pattern arrays fabricated through multialignment GSL achieved an exceptional 100% yield, compared to the 79.2% yield obtained through photolithography. GSL was implemented on various 2DMs to validate its universality, demonstrating repeatability by maintaining consistent dimensions after consecutive GSL cycles without mask degradation. Finally, the electrical performance of edge‐contact field‐effect transistors fabricated using GSL was evaluated, which confirms GSL as a practical approach to manufacture electronic devices utilizing 2DM. Consequently, this GSL method is expected to emerge as a promising patterning candidate for 2DM because it can overcome the critical processing vulnerabilities of conventional lithography to ensure high‐yield production.

items.title: Evaluating AI performance on end-to-end data science projects
items.abstract: Generative AI is used for knowledge work but many current AI evaluations focus on isolated tasks and constituent parts such as writing code, rather than end-to-end workflows. We test whether AI models can generate end-to-end data science projects. This requires AI models to select a dataset, develop a research question, write code to download, clean, and test data, create figures, and write a reproducible paper. To do this we collect 40 real end-to-end data science projects, then grade them according to a rubric. We use these to build an automated grading pipeline that evaluates data science projects and aligns with the grades that human graders give. For each of nine AI models we then generate five projects and use the automated grader to evaluate them. We find the extent to which generative AI models can complete end-to-end data science projects varies considerably by model. Most recent models did well on structured tasks, but there were considerable differences on tasks that needed judgment such as explaining measurement, writing abstracts, and citing sources. Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 averaged 87 per cent and OpenAI’s GPT-5.4 averaged 85 per cent, both around the level of an A for an undergraduate. No model was consistently the best across all aspects of the rubric. These findings suggest that while AI models could soon approximate entry-level data scientists on routine tasks, they require consistent verification and evaluation.

items.title: Enabling single-exposure metal logic with high-NA lithography
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of pitch 20 nm (P20) and pitch 18 nm (P18) metal logic designs, including regular tip-to-tip (T2T) and logic structures using bright-field masks in combination with dry metal-oxide resist. Patterning performance is evaluated across multiple source configurations and resist process conditions. For P20 T2T, we demonstrate a ∼13 nm T2T-CD (critical dimension) with local CD uniformity (LCDU) below 3 nm. For P18, single high-NA EUV exposure enables 18 nm T2T-CD with LCDU<3 nm. Further scaling is achieved using a directional etch at resist, reducing T2T-CD to ∼9 nm while maintaining LCDU ∼3 nm in P18 structure. To assess manufacturability, large-area defectivity is investigated using e-beam inspection after etch into hardmask for P20 metal logic structures. These results demonstrate the feasibility of single-patterning approaches for advanced metal logic and support the adoption of High-NA EUV for damascene integration.

items.title: Complementary Resistive Switching and IMPLY Logic Operations in Single Active Switching Material Standalone Memristive Devices
items.abstract: Complementary resistive switches (CRSs) are promising for nonvolatile memory, logic computing, and in-memory computing, but conventional implementations typically require two anti-serial memristive units, increasing device count and integration complexity. Here, the large surface-to-volume ratio of Ga2O3 nanowires is exploited to generate strong surface depletion effects. Coupled depletion regions between laterally bridged nanowires form an effective back-to-back depletion configuration, enabling complementary resistive switching in a single active switching material standalone memristive device. A Linear Technology Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (LTSpice) model is further developed to reproduce the measured electrical characteristics and verify Implies (IMPLY) logic operations, offering a compact route toward wide-bandgap oxide memristive logic, in-memory computing, and future electronics applications.

items.title: Charge‐Trapping Multilayer Electrets for Partial Discharge Mitigated AlN Substrates
items.abstract: ABSTRACT High electric fields within power devices can trigger partial discharge (PD), which can gradually degrade insulation materials, such as ceramic substrates and encapsulation compounds. This work counters and reduces electric fields using multilayer thin‐film electret structures incorporating , , , and AlN to mitigate PD in WBG power electronic packages. The proposed thin film structures can be conductively charged, allowing charges to be injected and trapped within the thin film stack. The stored charges generate electric fields and reduce intensified local fields that cause PD. The proposed electret design allows in‐situ conductive charging, unlike previous electrets that required pre‐charging through an external charging system. To evaluate the electric field suppression capabilities, PD measurements were performed under steep (high‐dV/dt), high‐voltage pulse excitations. The results show a decrease in PD activity, indicating a successful electric field reduction. Finite‐element simulation of the measured structure shows that the retained charge reduces the field at the triple point by about 32, and the measured apparent charge decreases in almost all conditions above the inception voltage. Overall, the proposed approach provides a promising way to improve insulation performance in high‐voltage WBG power modules.

items.title: Biologically inspired neuromorphic algorithms for low power learning
items.abstract: While neuromorphic computing offers a potential low power alternative to current resource-hungry AI, it requires fresh algorithmic approaches. The field needs a new generation of Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) that have not evolved with conventional hardware but instead align with characteristics of nascent neuromorphic platforms. With this goal in mind, we research biologically inspired networks that expand by incorporating fresh neurons to facilitate continual learning. This architectural plasticity is largely overlooked as a technique in conventional machine learning and is inspired by biological adult neurogenesis. To underpin our research, we provide a unifying definition and mathematical formulation for a group of associative memory networks that expand during learning. Our formulation enables theoretical network optimisation which demonstrates greater than 10,000 times improvement in memory capacity compared to previous work. We then direct our focus on the learning step itself and propose several new neurogenesis learning strategies that increase in memory recall accuracy from 69% to 96%, while retaining a fixed resource budget. Furthermore, through application of our findings to the more complex task of Class Incremental Learning (CIL), we are able demonstrate that dedicating separate resources to the independent learning of each class can help to regulate learning. Our consolidated findings include: methods to increase accuracy by reducing bias towards specific memories during learning; methods to reduce the computational cost of architectural plasticity during learning; and empirical demonstration that a modular network topology can be exploited to optimise neurogenesis. In summary, we extend existing neuromorphic research through the formal articulation, assessment, and advancement of learning strategies that incorporate architectural plasticity. The research responds directly to calls from the neuromorphic research community for original approaches to progress neuromorphic algorithm development.

items.title: Bibliometric Analysis of Global Research Trends on Simulation Studies of AlGaN/GaN High-Electron-Mobility Transistors Using the Scopus Database
items.abstract: Abstract As the design space of AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) grows increasingly complex, simulation has become an indispensable tool for understanding device physics and optimizing performance before fabrication. However, few studies have measured and analyzed the scientific publications on AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation from a global perspective. In this bibliometric study, our aim was to evaluate the global research trends in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation areas based on publication outputs, co-authorships among countries, and co-occurrences of author keywords. Using the Scopus database, a total of 4,492 journal articles and conference papers published between 1997 and 2026 were retrieved and analyzed using VOSviewer. Results have shown that since 2001, the number of publications has increased steadily, with the highest annual output recorded in 2025 (490 articles), resulting in a steady increase in the cumulative total publications. China (1,284 articles) and India (961 articles) are the leading contributors, followed by the USA (695 articles); however, Belgium, the UAE, and Singapore exhibit the highest rates of international collaboration. A keyword co-occurrence analysis of 61 keywords revealed six distinct thematic clusters, dominated by power/thermal management, device/HEMT core, modeling/RF, TCAD/gate, electric field, and machine learning. The most recently active keywords include TCAD simulation, gate leakage current, power amplifier, and S-parameter, suggesting a growing emphasis on simulation-driven design and RF performance in recent years. In conclusion, recent progress in AlGaN/GaN HEMT simulation research includes the following (but not limited to): (i) integration of advanced TCAD and physics-based models for trap dynamics and self-heating; (ii) AI-driven and machine learning approaches for device modeling; and (iii) continued exploration of p-GaN gate and enhancement-mode structures for high-power and high-frequency applications.

items.title: BF-IMNA: A Bit Fluid In-Memory Neural Architecture for Neural Network Acceleration
items.abstract: Mixed-precision quantization, which assigns precisions per-layer, per-network, per-channel, or per-parameter, is gaining traction for efficient Neural Network (NN) realization with higher throughput and lower energy. Unlike conventional fixed-precision accelerators, BF-IMNA advances the mixed-precision design space through an AP-based in-memory implementation. We present BF-IMNA, a bit fluid IMC accelerator for end-to-end Convolutional NN inference supporting static and dynamic mixed-precision without run-time reconfiguration overhead. At its heart are Associative Processors (APs), bit-serial word-parallel SIMD-like engines. We evaluate ImageNet inference with AlexNet, VGG16, and ResNet50 across SRAM and ReRAM CAM cells, mixed-precision configurations, and supply voltages. To demonstrate bit fluidity, we apply HAWQ-V3's published ResNet18 schedules to the BF-IMNA cost model and pair them with HAWQ-V3's published accuracies and model sizes. The results reveal an accuracy–Energy-Delay Product trade-off. The high-latency point is \(1.16\) points below INT8 accuracy with \(1.13\times\) better EDP, while the low-latency point has \(1.91\times\) better EDP and a \(45.5\%\) smaller model at a \(3.00\) -point accuracy reduction. At 500-MHz, true-batch-one comparison, BitFusion provides lower absolute energy and latency, while BF-IMNA provides lower average power at all five operating points, \(2106\times\) greater on-chip weight capacity ( \(32.8\times\) per unit modeled area), and larger relative energy reductions at aggressive INT4 and low-latency HAWQ points.
items.venue: ACM Journal on Emerging Technologies in Computing Systems

items.title: BCAT: A Block Causal Transformer for PDE Foundation Models for Fluid Dynamics
items.abstract: Background: Foundation models have demonstrated remarkable generalization in vision and language, but their accurate use for scientific computing remains challenging. For two-dimensional fluid-dynamics prediction, current transformer-based models are often hindered by limited context and rigid causality information, as they typically map fixed windows to the next step. Objectives: We aim to develop a unified architecture for heterogeneous fluid-dynamics families. The goal is to better capture the complex spatio-temporal dependencies inherent in nonlinear fluid dynamics. Methods: We introduce BCAT, a block-causal transformer for autoregressive prediction of two-dimensional fluid-dynamics solutions. Our approach adapts block-causal attention to next-frame prediction, leveraging previous frames as contextual priors. The model is trained on 69K trajectory sequences from PDEBench, PDEArena, and CFDBench using the Muon optimizer. Results: BCAT achieved an average relative 𝐿 2 error of 1.18% across the six evaluated fluid families, reducing error by 45% relative to a 3.4-times-larger baseline. In ablations, next-frame prediction was 3.5x more accurate than the corresponding nexttoken variant. A five-seed analysis, noisy-input stress test, long-rollout analysis, and physics diagnostics further characterize the model. Conclusions: The block-causal framework captures spatial interactions within frames while enforcing temporal causality across frames. BCAT provides an accurate and computationally efficient model for the two-dimensional fluid-dynamics benchmarks considered here.

items.title: Accelerating Quantum Chemistry with Emulated Double-Precision Matrix Multiplication on GPUs
items.abstract: The evaluation of exact exchange and the treatment of electron correlation remain major computational challenges in electronic-structure theory. Over the past decade, GPU computing has substantially accelerated these calculations, extending the scale and complexity of electronic-structure problems that can be addressed computationally. More recently, GPU architectures developed to meet the demands of artificial intelligence have introduced new opportunities for acceleration, with Tensor Cores providing reduced-precision arithmetic throughput far exceeding that of native double-precision (FP64) operations. Exploiting this performance advantage while preserving the numerical accuracy required in quantum chemistry remains a significant challenge. Here, we investigate the Ozaki-I and Ozaki-II floating-point emulation schemes in the RI-HF, RI-MP2, and RI-CCSD implementations of EXESS on NVIDIA GB200 GPUs. We demonstrate that Ozaki-II at 52-bit precision achieves numerical accuracy comparable to native FP64, delivering complete calculation speedups of up to 1.26× (cc-pVDZ) and 1.50× (cc-pVTZ) for RI-HF, 2.55× and 3.01× for RI-MP2, and 3.11× and 2.15× for RI-CCSD. The energy to solution improves by 1.22× and 2.21× for the representative RI-HF and RI-MP2 cc- pVTZ calculations and by 2.37× for the RI- CCSD cc-pVDZ calculation. Reducing the precision to 47 bits provides further acceleration while maintaining total energy deviations below 0.1 kcal mol -1 across all systems examined.

items.title: AI-Assistant Thermal Hotspot Prediction and Chip Placement Optimization for Semiconductor Packages
items.abstract: Semiconductor packages are becoming more complex due to the increasing integration of multiple chips and chiplets within a single package. This can lead to higher heat generation and uneven temperature distribution, resulting in the formation of thermal hotspots. Excessive temperature can affect the performance and reliability of semiconductor devices. Conventional thermal analysis methods generally require repeated simulations to evaluate different chip placement arrangements, which can increase the time and computational effort. This project proposes an AI-based thermal hotspot prediction and chip placement optimization system for semiconductor packages. The proposed approach uses HotSpot thermal simulation to generate temperature data for different chip placement configurations. The generated dataset is processed using Python or MATLAB and used to train a Machine Learning model. The trained model predicts the maximum temperature and identifies possible thermal hotspot regions for different placement arrangements. Based on the predicted temperature, suitable chip placement configurations are selected and validated using HotSpot simulation. The proposed system aims to reduce the effort required for evaluating multiple placement configurations and support improved thermal-aware chip placement
authors: Prathiksha P, Shamini Genisia D, Dhecika M
items.venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

items.title: AI ethics by design: implementing customizable guardrails for responsible AI development
items.abstract: This paper explores the development of an ethical guardrail framework for AI systems, emphasizing the importance of customizable guardrails that align with diverse user values and underlying ethics. We address the challenges of AI ethics by proposing a structure that integrates rules, policies, and AI assistants to ensure responsible AI behavior, while comparing the proposed framework to the existing state-of-the-art guardrails. By focusing on practical mechanisms for implementing ethical standards, we aim to enhance transparency, user autonomy, and continuous improvement in AI systems. Our approach accommodates ethical pluralism, offering a flexible and adaptable solution for the evolving landscape of AI governance. The paper concludes with strategies for resolving conflicts between ethical directives, underscoring the present and future need for robust, nuanced and context-aware AI systems.

items.title: ADAPTATION AND EVALUATION OF THE MEMBRAIN SYSTEM FOR PROFILE-GUIDED DATA PLACEMENT ON INTEL XEON MAX PROCESSORS
items.abstract: We investigate the efficient utilization of tiered HBM and DDR memory on Intel Xeon Max processors under constrained high-bandwidth memory capacity. Unlike conventional capacity-expansion architectures (DRAM + CXL/NVM), tiered memory management with an integrated HBM tier remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we adapt the MemBrain automated profile-guided data placement framework for Intel Xeon Max servers: implementing interprocedural allocation-site function cloning in the LLVM compiler, hardware monitoring of last-level cache misses via PEBS, and guided user-space memory placement via the Intel UMF library. We study data placement optimization strategies based on an exact combinatorial optimization model (knapsack problem) and heuristic selection algorithms. Experimental evaluation on the LULESH 2.0 and Graph500-BFS benchmarks demonstrates that profile-guided data placement achieves up to 98.4%–99.9% of pure HBM performance while utilizing only a fraction of its physical capacity.

items.title: A Scalable 5 kW Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) Source for Next-Generation EUV Lithography: Design, Thermal Management, and Spectral Purity Analysis
items.abstract: The semiconductor industry's reliance on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) lithography is currently bottlenecked by the Laser-Produced Plasma (LPP) source, which suffers from low conversion efficiency (CE~5%), tin debris, and massive power consumption (>1 MW). In this paper, we propose a scaled-up Microwave Discharge Plasma (MDPP) source as a possible alternative. By scaling a laboratory microwave-discharge approach to a 5 kW microwave input, we outline a design that delivers between about 5 W and 110 W of in-band EUV power, depending on a conversion efficiency (0.5% to 10%) that is not yet verified for xenon. We address the main engineering bottlenecks of MDPP through three solutions: (1) a water-cooled aluminium nitride (AlN) capillary, transparent to microwaves, to manage a 4,500 W thermal load, (2) magnetic confinement and a magnetic nozzle to shrink the emitting column and reach a geometric etendue of about 1.0 mm²·sr, and (3) a Zr filter and two Mo/Si mirrors that reach a spectral purity above 99.99% under stated assumptions. A source-to-machine analysis shows that, for a 20 W target at the intermediate focus, a 5 kW source needs a conversion efficiency of at least about 3.6% with hemispherical collection, and about 81% with the closed end-on capillary, so the source geometry must be chosen from the optics requirement. Our calculations also expose open problems: the plasma density needed for efficient 13.5 nm emission is far above what a 100 mTorr, 2.45 GHz discharge is known to reach, and the Zr filter and the collection geometry limit the usable power. The design is therefore a concept for further modeling and experiment, not a demonstrated source.
