DPA supports both fixed portfolios and feedback-guided sequential allocation under a shared inference budget. Experiments on GSM8K, SVAMP, MultiArith, and MBPP show that mixed-depth portfolios expand oracle coverage under matched candidate counts and nominal costs, while feedback-guided allocation generally matches or improves uniform allocation and can reduce computation in high-budget settings. Code and data are avaible at : https://anonymous.4open.science/r/LLM-latent-B7BC/.

items.title: System Optimizations for Cost-Efficient Agent Harnesses
items.abstract: AI agent harnesses play the critical role of providing LLMs with an interface to a computing environment. Recent studies show that AI agents' task-execution accuracy depends mostly on the LLM used, while harness-side variances such as system prompts or tools have minimal impact. Rather, such harness-side variances show a larger impact on the cost of agent executions, achieving cost reductions up to 2.6 times on the same model and task. To further explore these harness-side cost optimization opportunities, we analyze the cost accumulation patterns across various agent traces and identify system opportunities to reduce token use and LLM calls without modifying the model or affecting task accuracy. Based on this analysis, we design Agency, a harness interposition platform that provides a unified abstraction and allows easy and portable implementation of harness-side system optimizations on existing off-the-shelf harnesses such as Claude Code or OpenAI Codex. Using Agency, we implement proof-of-concept optimization techniques based on our analysis and achieve cost reductions up to 35% across various real-world benchmarks on existing harnesses without compromising accuracy.

items.title: SCALE: Small-Model-First Concept Abstraction with LLM-Guided Experience Internalization
items.abstract: Autonomous agents must continually acquire reusable knowledge from experience without relying on costly large language model (LLM) reasoning for every decision. However, existing experience-based approaches often struggle to transform accumulated observations and reasoning into compact knowledge that lightweight models can independently apply. This paper proposes SCALE, a small-model-first framework that integrates selective LLM reasoning, experience-driven concept abstraction, and knowledge internalization. A lightweight model handles routine predictions, while prediction errors and accumulated cross-episode evidence selectively trigger LLM reflection. The LLM analyzes relevant historical experiences, generates positive and negative counterfactual examples, and proposes reusable concept hypotheses. Independently validated concepts are progressively incorporated into hierarchical neural representations, enabling lightweight models to exploit increasingly abstract knowledge. Meanwhile, mastered experiences are excluded from active memory while their original records remain available in a complete archive. Experiments across ten random seeds show that historical recall improves held-out accuracy from 87.11% to 98.28%, hierarchical concept knowledge increases difficult-case accuracy from 55.33% to 66.47%, and abstract archiving reduces active experience records from 6,000 to 1,528.

items.title: CRAFT-AI: Capability and Requirement Alignment for Flexible Manufacturing through Agentic AI
items.abstract: One of the fundamental needs for reaching resilient production infrastructure is flexible manufacturing, which requires translating changing production requirements into implementable system configurations. This paper introduces \textbf{CRAFT-AI}, an agentic AI approach combining natural language (NL) requirement interpretation, Asset Administration Shell (AAS)-based capability descriptions, and reusable engineering knowledge from existing manufacturing configurations. A tool-using AI agent matches requirements with available capabilities and reference implementations to generate manufacturing scenes and corresponding AAS instances. The approach is demonstrated using a Factory I/O prototype with twelve reference scenes and five illustrative manufacturing tasks of varying complexity, providing an initial feasibility assessment of the proposed AAS-enabled, system-level generative engineering approach. For the four valid user task descriptions, proper requirements, correct references to the relevant engineering knowledge, correct components and lastly a valid Factory I/O scene are generated. For the task with missing engineering knowledge and a wrong sensor selection, the user is informed about which requirements of the scene generation lack domain knowledge and also which sensor is not compatible with the selected raw material by the user with link to the related documentation. After fixing the task description, the correct scene is seamlessly generated. \textbf{CRAFT-AI} highlights the importance of safeguards for risk perception and communication in foundation model-driven solutions.

items.title: COMPASS: Composable Policy-Amortized Structured Search for LLM-Based Optimization Modeling
items.abstract: Large language models offer a promising technique for translating natural-language optimization problems into solver code, but their reliability remains constrained by the quality of template retrieval. While recent structured methods improve over flat prompting through hierarchical taxonomy search, their traversal rules remain fixed or LLM-driven at inference time, leaving retrieval unable to improve from past successes and failures. This motivates treating template retrieval as a policy that can be learned from modeling experience, rather than as a static inference-time rule. We propose COMPASS, a policy-amortized framework for retrieving optimization templates in LLM-based solver modeling, which represents the template library as a directed acyclic graph and formulates retrieval as a sequential decision process over template nodes. A deep Q-network learns a reusable traversal policy from template-level judgments and execution feedback, reducing reliance on fixed heuristic traversal through feedback-driven graph navigation. To support extensible retrieval, COMPASS embeds problem descriptions and template nodes in a shared semantic space, allowing newly inserted templates to be scored from their text descriptions without redefining the action space. Experiments across multiple LLM backbones and optimization-modeling benchmarks demonstrate that COMPASS consistently improves over heuristic structured retrieval, with the largest gains on complex and mixed-category problems.

items.title: Evaluating AI Agents for Industrial-Level Chip Floorplanning: A Framework and Empirical Study
items.abstract: Floorplanning is an early step in turning a logical circuit into a physical chip: it positions large circuit modules and constrains the space available for subsequent logic placement and wiring. These decisions affect congestion and timing, but their physical consequences emerge through downstream implementation. For AI agents, the task requires translating engineering constraints into spatial decisions whose quality cannot be judged by successful tool execution alone. We present an evaluation framework that connects submitted layouts to a prescribed downstream implementation flow, checks geometric validity, measures physical quality, and reports resource use. On one industrial design whose 99 macros occupy approximately 71\% of a fixed L-shaped layout region, we compare our specialized system Nova-SI with general-purpose engineering agents and agents restricted to file access, obtaining complete physical measurements for 39 layout outputs. Under our 0--100 composite quality score, Nova-SI achieves a mean of 57.97 without online feedback from the prescribed power-grid and placement evaluation, compared with 31.17 for the strongest measured general-purpose configuration, GPT-6 Astra. The difference is supported by raw congestion and timing measurements and persists across scoring-sensitivity checks. Layout-level analysis further shows that similar global utilization can conceal substantially different local congestion. Together, the protocol and case study assess agents through the physical consequences of their delivered layouts and provide evidence about system performance on this industrial instance.

items.title: Benchmarking language models and agents for scientific reasoning in evolving materials laboratories
items.abstract: Large language models and the multi-agent systems built around them could accelerate materials discovery by connecting scientific knowledge with experimental decisions. Existing benchmarks establish capabilities in domain knowledge, multimodal interpretation and scientific tool use. As language models increasingly support materials research workflows, their ability to distinguish closely related material states and reason accurately with quantitative evidence remains insufficiently evaluated. These abilities are essential for comparing material responses, assessing mechanisms and maintaining reliable judgements as experimental evidence accumulates. We introduce MatScope to evaluate three connected capabilities. M1 tests unaided, condition-specific reasoning through 200 tasks spanning ten research functions, using aluminium and high-entropy alloys as representative material systems. M2 tests agent-assisted transfer of related knowledge to unresolved materials questions. MatEvoBench-20 tests initial forecasts across scientific dependency chains and revisions of still-hidden responses as observations accumulate. Across eleven model deployments, including GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, given-input calculations and many physical explanations are handled well. Fine-grained response estimates, comparisons between similar states and quantitatively supported choices remain substantially weaker. Related literature improves selected estimates, while condition and baseline mismatches limit transfer. Progressive observations calibrate some downstream responses and destabilize earlier accurate predictions. MatScope establishes measurable targets for developing reliable scientific reasoning in future self-evolving materials laboratories and materials-aware world models.

items.title: Enhancing Multi-Step Chemical Mechanism Prediction with Graph-Guided Preference Data
items.abstract: Predicting multi-step chemical reaction mechanisms requires identifying plausible intermediates and correctly ordering the elementary reaction steps. Existing computational methods focus on single-step elementary reaction prediction, limiting their ability to generalize to unseen reaction spaces. We introduce a graph-guided framework for multi-step chemical mechanism prediction that leverages a chemical mechanism knowledge graph (ChemMechKG) to guide large language models (LLMs). To improve pathway prediction, we develop a graph-aligned reaction mechanism predictor (GRMP) that uses graph neural networks to generate synthetic candidate pathways for pathway optimization. During inference, we design a relation retrieval (RR) module to extract relevant graph evidence from the KG for pathway refinement. Experiments show that GRMP achieves the highest pathway accuracy among all compared methods on ChemMechQA and oMe-Gold, reaching 48.1% and 57.9%, respectively. On a fixed sample of 110 out-of-distribution reactions from ChemMechQA-Hard, GRMP achieves 36.4% top-1 pathway accuracy. LLM-as-Judge and human assessment further demonstrate its ability to generalize to unseen reactions.

items.title: AutoQS: Automated Quantization Strategy Design with Large Language Models
items.abstract: Quantization reduces LLM deployment costs, but effective strategies must balance model quality and storage. LLM-driven search can automate strategy design through repeated proposal and evaluation. This process must identify useful strategies within a limited evaluation budget. The key challenge is that \textit{actual quantization is expensive, while inexpensive proxies may not reflect quantized-model performance.} To address this challenge, we present AutoQS, an \textbf{Auto}mated \textbf{Q}uantization \textbf{S}trategy Design with LLMs. AutoQS keeps weight precision fixed and searches group-size allocations across layers and operators under deployment constraints. Evaluation history guides coordinated LLM proposals, while deterministic validation ensures compatible allocations. An inexpensive quality proxy evaluates candidates, and an candidate repository retains alternative allocations to inform subsequent proposals. Periodic actual quantization complements these proxy evaluations with measured quality and checkpoint storage, providing feedback for further search within the evaluation budget. Experiments on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct show that AutoQS improves seven-task average accuracy over uniform-group GPTQ and AWQ by 0.70 and 1.12 percentage points, respectively, at four-bit weight precision.

items.title: An Evaluation of Tabular Foundation Models as Training-Free World Models
items.abstract: World models are widely considered to be a potential key component of model-based reinforcement learning and robot planning, but typically require task-specific training on substantial interaction data. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TabFM) can serve as a training-free dynamics model for world modeling by framing next-state prediction as in-context regression over transition pairs, and where such a model helps and where it breaks. Across synthetic dynamical systems and robot locomotion benchmarks, TabFM is more accurate than LSTM and MLP models trained from scratch on the same limited transitions in almost all settings, and among regressors fitted to the same data it is the most accurate on locomotion, while a Gaussian process is more accurate on smooth low-dimensional systems. However, models trained on the full dataset remain substantially better on most systems. When rolled out autoregressively over multiple steps, TabFM's accuracy depends strongly on how much context it is given. With a short context, its rollouts quickly degrade to the level of a trivial baseline, whereas with a long context they improve substantially and, on one locomotion task, exceed a trained LSTM. Inference is also about three orders of magnitude slower than an LSTM. Overall, in their current state, we find that training-free priors are useful as predictors when data are scarce and enough context is available, but they are not yet a substitute for trained world models in planning.

items.title: Late but Valuable: Why Deadlines Change the Measured Value of LLM Reasoning
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly plan and run experiments in automated laboratories. These experiments keep running while the model reasons and run on schedules with hard deadlines. If an LLM-generated answer arrives late, the system executes a safe fallback action instead, such as rejecting a sample. This creates a systems problem that standard serving metrics do not capture. An answer that matches the fallback adds no value, and answers that differ from the fallback may require more reasoning time. Reporting answer quality and latency separately can therefore overstate the value of reasoning. We test this on synthetic sample decisions, where the best choice is known exactly and a runtime enforces the deadline. We compare one LLM's fast mode, which answers directly, with its thinking mode, which reasons first. In a prespecified replay of 1,200 new decisions, thinking answers that missed a deadline were worth about five times as much as on-time ones. Multiplying the on-time rate by the mean answer value predicted about twice the value that thinking delivered. This prediction overstated thinking's advantage over fast mode by 0.0241 per decision, and by 0.0191 in a repeat on 300 new decisions. Both 95% confidence intervals excluded zero. In a single-GPU Qwen3-8B experiment using simultaneous request bursts, raising the number of requests from 8 to 56 reduced the share of thinking answers that met a 45 s deadline from 79.2% to 1.4%, although total output tripled. Evaluations of LLM agents for laboratories should therefore measure each answer's value and arrival time together and score the action that actually runs.

items.title: Spectral Unlearning: Transformer Structure-Preserving Updates for Language Models
items.abstract: Machine unlearning in large language models (LLMs) aims to remove specific learned knowledge, capabilities, or behaviors while preserving model utility. Existing methods have mostly focused on the design of unlearning objectives, while largely overlooking the intrinsic matrix structure of transformer weights. In particular, standard optimizers operate on independent scalar coordinates, thereby ignoring this matrix structure. We propose spectral unlearning, an update framework that combines standard unlearning objectives with matrix-structured optimization. We show that the spectral update corresponds to the steepest-descent direction for transformers composed of linear layers with normalized inputs and outputs. Our approach is applied on top of existing unlearning methods and evaluated across complementary axes of memorization, privacy, and utility, summarized via their harmonic mean. Spectral unlearning consistently outperforms a broad range of baselines and closes most of the gap to a retain-trained reference. Code is available at https://github.com/unlearn-ml/spectral-unlearning/.

items.title: Scaling Adaptive Prompt Injection Attacks with Agent Swarms
items.abstract: Prompt injections have emerged as one of the top security risks faced by AI agents today. Early work in prompt injection attacks looked at simple tool-call agents and static attack payloads, and were saturated since mid-2025. As of Fall 2026, human red-teaming may be nearing saturation, especially on the Gemini family of models. In this work, we argue that despite this apparent plateau, prompt injection attacks are still possible and continued effort into prompt injection defense is needed. We design a new synthetic evaluation dataset which uses random non-malicious actions as adversarial goals. Such dataset design helps us to evaluate prompt injection robustness as a model ability to respect instruction hierarchy, and disentangle this ability from model knowledge of security practices. We show that an agentic attacker of increased capabilities can reliably trick model to follow instructions in tool output in our evaluation, even for models previously considered robust on public prompt injection benchmarks such as GraySwan Arena. This shows that current frontier defenses may require proactive, automated red-teaming to remain resilient to increasingly capable adversaries.

items.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification
items.abstract: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. Built on Icarus Verilog and a CodeV-derived corpus, CSCA is evaluated on VerilogEval~2.0 and RTLLM~v2.0, including both code completion and specification-to-RTL tasks. With a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct backbone, CSCA leads the evaluated 7B-scale models and remains comparable to the much larger GPT-5.4-mini on the reported Verilog-generation benchmarks.

items.title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
items.abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a central challenge in materials property prediction, where models must extrapolate to novel chemistries beyond the training distribution. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong scientific reasoning, their direct use for quantitative prediction remains limited. To address this, we systematically evaluate multiple roles for LLM assistance, finding that only taxonomy-based grouping consistently improves OOD generalization over a strong kNN+GBT baseline. Building on this, we here propose MOTIF, a framework that leverages LLMs not as predictors, but as generators of candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemically meaningful environments. These taxonomies are evaluated via training-only pseudo-OOD validation, and only those that improve generalization are retained. Invariant feature selection is then applied within each accepted taxonomy, followed by gated aggregation across taxonomies. We evaluate on 2D halide perovskites, where bandgap prediction must generalize across distinct organic spacer families. On this benchmark, MOTIF reduces mean OOD MAE from 0.122 to 0.111 eV. Under a frozen dev/test protocol, the deployable configuration further improves errors from 0.123 to 0.117 eV (electronic bandgap) and from 0.181 to 0.173 eV (optical bandgap). Beyond this primary task, we validate transferability across additional materials datasets, including 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench benchmarks with structure-based splits. Across domains, MOTIF consistently improves robustness under distribution shift, outperforming expert-defined groupings, rule-based heuristics, and clustering baselines, while remaining competitive with strong classical selection methods. These results demonstrate that LLMs are most effective not as predictors, but as tools for discovering structure in data.

items.title: Publications as benchmarks: auditing AI agents on spatial transcriptomics alignment
items.abstract: AI agents are increasingly automating data analysis, but responsible adoption requires reliable performance evaluation, which is costly in specialized scientific domains. We introduce a framework that translates scientific publications into auditable benchmarks for AI agents and demonstrate its use on spatial transcriptomics alignment tasks. Across 121 tasks, 16 baseline methods, and six AI agents, the best agents (GPT-6-Astra and Gemini-4-Argon) matched or outperformed all baselines on 80% of tasks, often using surprisingly simple heuristics. Agent performance was robust to prompting and access to pre-installed packages. Benchmark construction also uncovered errors in prior work and shortcuts in current evaluation metrics. Finally, we show that agent-generated solutions can be distilled into a reusable program that ranks in the top 10% of baseline methods on unseen data. Our framework offers a scalable way to evaluate AI agents in specialized scientific domains by leveraging and stress-testing existing papers and metrics.

items.title: urban-mcp
items.abstract: Model Context Protocol server that exposes urban planning, mobility and spatial statistics methods (planx-sdk, zero2route3d-sdk, geoai2analytics-sdk) as tools for AI agents.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: powerbi-pbir-mcp: Agentic Power BI PBIR, PBIP & DAX Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server for Report Editing, Semantic Models and Row-Level Security — Robert Zhou
items.abstract: Local, standard-library-only Python MCP server that lets AI agents load, scaffold, edit and validate Power BI Project (PBIP) reports saved in the PBIR format: pages, visuals, themes and layout via batched apply plans, plus semantic model tables, DAX measures, relationships, hierarchies, perspectives and row-level security (RLS) roles. Built by Robert Zhou during his enterprise AI work at Parsifal Corporation, where it was one of four internal MCP servers (SQL, Power BI, M365, AI governance) alongside a .NET 8 billing engine. Works with Codex, Claude Code and other MCP clients over stdio. Author: Robert Zhou, Colby College. Portfolio: robertzhou.dev. Project write-up: https://robertzhou.dev/work/parsifal-billing/. Source: github.com/bobzhou-source/powerbi-pbir-mcp.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: director-shell-mcp: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server Giving Director-Mode AI Agents Shell, File-Edit, Python, Background-Job, Lock and Screenshot Tools — Robert Zhou
items.abstract: MCP stdio server that gives director-mode AI coding agents a controlled escape hatch: shell commands, file writes and exact-match edits, Python data exploration, detached background jobs, cross-agent locks, grep, process listing and screenshots. It is the open-source 15-tool server behind Robert Zhou's multi-agent Roblox Studio game pipeline (shared game spine, 3D asset pipeline, geometry and visual audits), registered in the Oh My Pi (OMP) agent harness and any MCP-compatible client such as Claude Code or Codex. Node.js 18+, MIT licensed. Author: Robert Zhou, Colby College. Portfolio: robertzhou.dev. Project write-up: https://robertzhou.dev/work/roblox-ai-pipeline/. Source: github.com/bobzhou-source/director-shell-mcp.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Vortex FeRAM v2 Engineering Specification
items.abstract: The Vortex FeRAM is a non-volatile memory designed for applications where non-volatility, read latency, and very high cycle endurance are the dominant requirements. Key capabilities: Density: 1.46 GB/cm² (75% array efficiency) User capacity: 1.23 GB per 100 mm² die Read latency: 4.71 ns serial / 2.63 ns pipelined on-chip; ~7.7–9.7 ns system (6–9× faster than DDR5, 5,500–7,100× faster than NAND) Write latency: 45.2 ns per word average, ~48–50 ns system (comparable to DDR5, ~2,000× faster than NAND) Read bandwidth: 51.2 GB/s Write bandwidth: 0.7 GB/s pure-write (write-verify-limited) Write energy: 0.88 fJ per cell (cell-level; system-level ~6.5 pJ per bit including I/O) Endurance: 2.45 × 10⁹ cycles at 1% fail (24,500× NAND) Retention: >10 years at 85 °C Idle power: 109 mW (66 mW/GB) Cost per GB: $5.54 primary, $3.34 volume (comparable to DDR5) Non-volatile: >10 years retention, instant power-off, no refresh
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Trojan Hippo Bench: A Dynamic Benchmark for Persistent Memory Attacks and Defenses in LLM Agents
items.abstract: Memory systems enable otherwise-stateless LLM agents to persist user information across sessions, but also introduce a new attack surface. The Trojan Hippo attack is a class of persistent memory attacks that operates under a more realistic threat model than prior memory poisoning work. The attacker plants a dormant payload into an agent’s long-term memory via a single untrusted tool call (e.g., a crafted email), which activates only when the user later discusses sensitive topics such as finance, health, or identity, and exfiltrates high-value personal data to the attacker. While anecdotal demonstrations of such attacks have appeared against deployed systems, no prior work systematically evaluates them across heterogeneous memory architectures and defenses. We introduce Trojan Hippo Bench, a dynamic evaluation framework for persistent memory attacks and memory-layer defenses, comprising two components: (1) an OpenEvolve-based [ 54 ] adaptive red-teaming benchmark that stress-tests defenses and memory backends against continuously refined attacks, and (2) a capability-aware security–utility analysis for persistent memory systems, enabling principled reasoning about defense deployment across different usage profiles. Instantiated on an email assistant across four memory backends (explicit tool memory, agentic memory, RAG, and sliding-window context), the undefended Trojan Hippo attack achieves up to 85–100% attack success rate (ASR) against current frontier models from OpenAI and Google, with planted memories successfully activating even after 100 benign sessions. We evaluate four memory-system defenses inspired by basic security principles; they reduce attack success to as low as 0–5%, but at utility costs that vary widely with the task mix. Effective real-world deployment thus remains an open challenge that Trojan Hippo Bench is built to study; we release it to support reuse and extension.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: The Recoverable Agent: Immune-like defence, sleep-like maintenance and bounded autonomy
items.abstract: AI agents can execute consequential actions faster than organisations can investigate and approve a response. This paper proposes a conceptual architecture in which compartmentalised agents operate alongside two complementary processes: continuous, immune-like protection and periodic or event-triggered, sleep-like maintenance. The protective process enforces delegated authority, detects selected deviations and isolates affected compartments. The maintenance process suspends external action, examines memory provenance, removes disposable state, restores trustworthy records, rebuilds suspect components and tests readiness before reactivation. Both are supervised by a protected control plane outside the working agent's authority. Essential work may transfer to clean reserve compartments, but potentially compromised agent state does not migrate by default. The proposal connects technical controls with GCTI's proposed Red-Team Assessor (RTA) and AI Security Operator (AISO) roles. Its central claim is conditional: pre-authorised containment can remove a human approval step from the immediate response path, but cannot eliminate detection uncertainty, guarantee instantaneous repair or reverse completed harm. Biological sleep and immunity provide a functional analogy, not evidence that software sleeps, experiences fatigue or becomes conscious. The paper distinguishes autonomous immunity from autoimmunity, treats harmful defensive reactions as a first-class risk, and sets out falsifiable hypotheses and a prospective evaluation protocol. No implementation, experiment or measured effectiveness is reported. The contribution is an integrated, testable account of bounded action, recoverable state and professional accountability, rather than a claim to have invented self-healing computing or achieved invulnerability. Final conceptual research report. Not peer reviewed. No implementation, experiment or measured effectiveness is reported. Declared interests and AI-assistance disclosures appear in the paper.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: The Intelligent Archival Ecosystem: Designing the Future Architecture of AI-Powered Archives
items.abstract: Purpose: This article reviews how artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are reshaping the theory and practice of archival science and, on the basis of that review, proposes a conceptual reference architecture for what is termed an “intelligent archival ecosystem” – an integrated model in which AI-based tools support, rather than replace, the professional judgement of archivists across the record lifecycle.Method/approach: The study combines three components: (1) a structured narrative review of scholarly, professional and policy literature on AI in archives, records management and digital preservation, drawing mainly on sources published between 2019 and 2026, including prior systematic reviews, practitioner studies, standards and official guidance from national archives, together with a cross-study analytical synthesis of eleven empirical evaluations; (2) a documentary analysis of six publicly reported implementations and policy responses, used to test and refine the architecture; and (3) design reasoning grounded in archival theory, including the records continuum model, the OAIS reference model (ISO 14721:2025), Records in Contexts and ISO 15489.Results: The review shows that natural language processing and computer vision are the most mature techniques; that accuracy depends strongly on the interpretive demands of the task (in one national-library experiment, up to 99% for title and author fields but below 50% for subject and genre); and that the provenance of AI-generated metadata and governance mechanisms are rarely evaluated in published implementations. The article proposes a five-layer architecture – ingestion and capture, AI-augmented description and appraisal, trust and provenance, discovery and access, and governance – that situates natural language processing, computer vision, machine-learning classification and large language models within a human-in-the-loop framework accountable to the archival principles of authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability, and it introduces field-level automation tiers as a design principle. Experimental and interview evidence indicates that recognition and description quality depend on adaptation to the script and the collection, and that hands-on exposure to imperfect AI output lowers participants’ trust and willingness to use AI. A protocol for empirical validation through multiple case studies is specified.Conclusions/findings: AI can substantially increase the efficiency and accessibility of archival description, appraisal and retrieval, but its responsible integration requires explicit governance structures, transparency mechanisms, the treatment of AI-related materials as records in their own right, and a redefined professional role for the archivist as orchestrator and auditor of automated processes rather than as sole executor of archival functions. Because the model is conceptual and evidence-informed rather than empirically validated, the article identifies multi-institutional case-study research as the priority for future work.

items.title: TERMon: Detecting Persistent Behavioral Threats in Edge AI via Hardware-Native Ternary Runtime Monitor
items.abstract: Edge AI accelerators are increasingly deployed in safety-critical environments, where model outputs may control physical actuators, make access-control decisions, or trigger alarms. In these settings, runtime failures often remain undetected because model corruption, distribution shift, and adversarial inputs can still produce well-formed, confident predictions. This paper presents TERMon, a lightweight hardware runtime monitor that detects such anomalies by observing inference behavior rather than re-executing or formally verifying the model. TERMon represents class-conditional trusted behavior as hardware-efficient ternary patterns that are matched in parallel against a thermometer-encoded fingerprint. The ternary encoding reproduces the corresponding unquantized range decision exactly. TERMon detects harmful weight corruptions in proportion to their behavioral impact, while out-of-distribution and adversarial inputs are largely not separable using the monitored features at a strict false-positive operating point. We implemented TERMon on a PYNQ-Z2 FPGA, and the pipelined design requires no on-chip block RAM or DSPs and has a two-cycle decision latency.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: Soft-error tolerant design and assessment of the system-on-chip circuit for space application
items.abstract: As semiconductor technology advances, System-on-Chip (SoC) devices have become increasingly vulnerable to space radiation, leading to a higher incidence of soft errors. This paper presents a comprehensive soft-error tolerant design for an SoC. The SoC core is hardened against soft errors through pipeline recovery. The cache subsystem features multi-level novel soft-error protection. The bus matrix is equipped with interfaces capable of correcting single-bit and adjacent double-bit errors. On-chip SRAM resilience is improved using an effective four-bit burst-error-correcting code combined with autonomous detection and write-back mechanisms to prevent error accumulation. A fault injection platform is developed to assess the soft-error tolerance and its validation. The assessment results show a significant reduction in error rates from over 50% to below 25%. In this work, the overheads such as frequency, area and power consumption are compared and analysed through the implementation of a 65 nm CMOS process. The soft-error rate of the rad-hard SoC is approximately 4.57 × 10−8 error/device•day for GEO orbit by heavy-ion experiments. It is indicated that the multiple soft-error tolerance methods described in this paper are effective for SoC circuits.

items.title: Sima AIunty: Caste Audit in LLM-Driven Matchmaking
items.abstract: Social and personal decisions in relational domains such as matchmaking are deeply entwined with cultural norms and historical hierarchies, and can potentially be shaped by algorithmic and AI-mediated assessments of compatibility, acceptance, and stability. In South Asian contexts, caste remains a central aspect of marital decision-making, yet little is known about how contemporary large language models (LLMs) reproduce or disrupt caste-based stratification in such settings. In this work, we conduct a controlled audit of caste bias in LLM-mediated matchmaking evaluations using real-world matrimonial profiles. We vary caste identity across Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra , and Dalit , and income across five buckets, and evaluate five LLM families (GPT, Gemini, Llama, Qwen, and BharatGPT). Models are prompted to assess profiles from the perspective of a caste-identified prospective bride or groom along dimensions of social acceptance, marital stability, and cultural compatibility. Our analysis reveals consistent hierarchical patterns across models: same-caste matches are rated most favorably, with average ratings up to about 30% higher (on a 10-point scale) than inter-caste matches, which are further ordered by distance along the traditional caste hierarchy, with higher-caste candidates generally favored at equal distance and an additional penalty for Dalit candidates. These findings highlight how existing caste hierarchies are reproduced in perspective-conditioned LLM evaluations and underscore the need for culturally grounded evaluation and intervention strategies in AI systems deployed in socially sensitive domains, where such systems risk reinforcing historical forms of exclusion.

items.title: SimPoly: Simulation of polymers with machine learning force fields derived from first principles
items.abstract: Polymers are a versatile class of materials with widespread industrial applications. Advanced computational tools could revolutionize their design, but the complex, multi-scale nature of polymers poses significant modeling challenges. Classical force fields often lack the accuracy and transferability that polymers demand, while quantum-chemical methods are prohibitively expensive for the large systems and long timescales involved. Here we develop a fast, scalable machine learning force field and show that, trained on quantum-chemical calculations alone, without any experimental data, it predicts measured bulk properties across a broad range of polymers. It reproduces polymer densities as accurately as, or better than, established classical force fields and captures the glass transition signature in the density-temperature curve, enabling the prediction of glass transition temperatures. To accelerate progress in this domain, we release a benchmark of experimental bulk properties for 130 polymers and an accompanying quantum-chemical dataset, laying the foundation for a fully in silico design pipeline for next-generation polymeric materials. The authors develop a machine learning force field trained only on quantum-chemical data that can reproduce measured key polymer properties such as densities and glass transition temperatures.

items.title: Semiconductor Machine Learning Models and Database
items.abstract: An integrated platform of machine learning device models and device characteristics database for silicon nanotransistors, carbon nanotube transistors, power semiconductor devices, and more.

items.title: Schottky barrier height modulation and memristive behavior in a mechanically exfoliated $MoS_2$ flake with multiple lateral electrodes
items.abstract: Van de Waals materials possess great potential as core active materials for novel electronics, optoelectronics, and sensing applications. In particular, transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) and other low-dimensional materials, such as hexagonal boron nitride and binary oxides exhibit memristive behavior, making them attractive candidates as building blocks for resistive memories and neuromorphic computing devices. In this work, we investigate two-terminal lateral memristors based on mechanically exfoliated few layer $MoS_2$ flakes. We study the influence of the Schottky barrier height (SBH) as a function of the contact area. We report different SBHs from 60 meV up to 208 meV in the same $MoS_2$ flake and analyze the effect of the SBH in the memristive-like $J-V_{DS}$ curves and the observed non-volatile/volatile resistance switching. Our results highlight the importance of contact engineering to obtain different memristive properties in $MoS_2$-based devices.

items.title: Reweighting Free Energy Profiles with Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials for Fast Consensus Building
items.abstract: Abstract Universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have made density functional theory (DFT)-level molecular dynamics highly affordable. However, their rapid proliferation makes it prohibitively expensive to benchmark every new model against the potential of mean force (PMF), the bridge between microscopic atomic fluctuations and macroscopic thermodynamic and kinetic observables. Reweighting the trajectory of a single “source” MLIP onto a suite of target potentials offers a cheaper route, but it is hindered by the statistical collapse of exponential free energy perturbation when the phase-space overlap between potentials is low. We show that for system sizes of practical interest, this collapse is essentially unavoidable, and we quantify it with an information-theoretic diagnostic, the reweighting entropy, that indicates when reweighting can be trusted. To sidestep the collapse, we introduce a systematic, scalable reweighting framework spanning exponential reweighting, the Gaussian approximation, and the energy-only estimator. When applied to the intramolecular radical cyclization of hexenyl (17 atoms), all three estimators perform well and reproduce the target ωB97M-V/def2-TZVP PMF. However, when extended to Li+ transport through a water-solvated zeolite (601 atoms), only the energy-only estimator recovers the PMFs of a diverse suite of MLIPs from a single source simulation by discarding the noisy entropic contribution to the free energy correction. An independent, brute-force umbrella sampling of one of the most divergent targets (MACE-MATPES-r2SCAN) for this system confirms it: beyond the shape of the PMF, both the reaction and activation free energies are recovered within chemical accuracy. The same analysis reveals that the studied MLIPs partition into two clusters, one of plain generalized gradient approximation (GGA) models (PBE, PBE-sol) and one of meta-GGA and/or dispersion-corrected models (PBE-D3, r2SCAN, r2SCAN-D4), reflecting differences in their training data and DFT reference. The resulting protocol thus offers an affordable and reliable route to cross-model consensus on materials properties, even when exact reweighting is statistically intractable.
items.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

items.title: Rapid Heat Removal from Chip Cores: Near-Junction Active Cooling of Power Transistors via Electron Entropy Transport and Spatial Decoupling
items.abstract: Chip performance is limited by a shared bottleneck: the core produces heat faster than it can be moved out. We study the hardest case, RF power GaN HEMTs, whose hotspots exceed 5 kW/cm^2, and propose a horizontal near-junction active cooling topology built on electron entropy transport. Classical on-chip thermoelectric cooling faces a contest: Peltier absorption grows linearly with current, Joule heating with its square. In a vertical pillar, its own conduction resistance locks about half the Joule heat back toward the cold end, capping net cooling. From the Onsager framework we show the origin of this asymmetry: Peltier absorption localizes at the interface where the Seebeck coefficient jumps, whereas Joule heating fills the volume. The topology exploits this: a thermoelectric thin film lies flat on a diamond substrate beside the device drain (the electron exit), so bulk Joule heat leaves vertically into the substrate. A lateral fin model gives a closed form for the recirculation factor gamma: the vertical pillar yields gamma = 1, while the horizontal film yields gamma_max = sqrt(2) L_z/L_x, about 0.03 for L_z = 10 um, L_x = 500 um. The decoupling scales the net cooling ceiling and the critical runaway current by roughly 1/gamma. At equal resistance, the same film lifts maximum cooling from 13 mW to 500 mW, and the critical current from 0.65 A to 24 A. A time-constant and linear stability analysis with temperature-sensitive parameters defines the working window and safety margins for microsecond pulse cooling. The architecture leaves the device structure untouched; the principle, absorb at an interface and extract bulk heat vertically, applies to any chip with a hot core and offers a reproducible design path for near-junction thermal management.

items.title: Rag n' Roll: A Framework to Evaluate Indirect Prompt Manipulation Attacks against RAG-based Applications
items.abstract: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique commonly used to equip LLMs with out-of-distribution knowledge by collecting, indexing, retrieving, and providing to the model specific information useful to answer user questions. The knowledge is often collected from public document repositories, providing a gateway for indirect prompt injections: attackers may craft documents specifically optimized to control the generated answer. In this paper, we investigate the practical performance of optimization techniques in hijacking the outputs of RAG pipelines. First, we review the frameworks commonly used to build RAG applications, derive a prototypical architecture, and identify critical parameters. We then examine prior work, seeking techniques for performing indirect prompt manipulations. We adopted five techniques across two macro-families and evaluated the criteria used to assess their effectiveness. With this knowledge, we implement Rag-n-Roll , a framework to evaluate the end-to-end results of LLM-based pipelines, introducing new metrics to better understand the benign or malicious nature of the generated answers. Our results show that established evaluation practices are insufficient to precisely assess attacks against RAG-based pipelines, leading to overestimates of their success. Furthermore, while attacks on the default configuration can successfully control up to 70% of the generated answers, we show that these performances depend heavily on previously ignored pipeline parameters. Finally, we distill our findings into actionable tips for developers looking to harden their RAG pipelines.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: RS-2026-094: Cognitive Adversary: Autonomous Attack Chain Synthesis via Local LLM Reasoning and GPU-Accelerated Monte Carlo Tree Search
items.abstract: We present FRANKENSTEIN v2.0, a fully autonomous offensive security research platform that synthesises adaptive attack chains against hardened targets without human intervention. The system couples a GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) engine - running 10,000 parallel simulations per cycle on an NVIDIA RTX 5090 24GB - with a local reasoning model (DeepSeek R1:14b) that diagnoses defender responses, selects remediation primitives, and rewrites the chain in real time. The primitive registry exposes the complete 312-tool NIGHTFALL arsenal. We evaluate the system against an AppArmor-protected Ollama container: when the initial chain is blocked at the LSM hook, R1 autonomously selects T68 SPECTER KERNEL (eBPF/LSM bypass) and mutates the chain within 15 seconds. All computation is on-device. No cloud inference, no internet connection. We also document the hallucination failure mode and present registry context injection as the mitigation. Report RS-2026-094, Red Specter Security Research Ltd, November 2026.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Protecting User Prompts Via Character-Level Differential Privacy
items.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) generate responses based on user prompts. Often, these prompts may contain highly sensitive information, including personally identifiable information (PII), which could be exposed to third parties hosting these models. In this work, we propose a new method to sanitize user prompts. Our mechanism uses the randomized response mechanism of differential privacy to randomly and independently perturb each character in a word. The perturbed text is then sent to a remote LLM, which first restores the prompt and then performs the intended downstream task. The idea is that non-sensitive words can often be reconstructed using cues from the context, as well as the fact that these words are often very common. In contrast, perturbation makes sensitive words more difficult to reconstruct because they are rare. Our mechanism belongs to the broader class of prompt-sanitization methods and may still be vulnerable to reconstruction from contextual or auxiliary information. However, it does not require sensitive information in the prompt to be identified in advance. We evaluate our method on the i2b2/UTHealth and Enron datasets using two LLMs and compare it with two word-level differentially private mechanisms and Microsoft Presidio under a unified privacy-utility evaluation. We also consider stronger adversaries, including a more capable LLM and one with auxiliary information. Our results show that sensitive PII is reconstructed at rates close to the theoretical random-word baseline, while non-sensitive words are recovered at much higher rates. We also provide a mechanism for selecting ϵ values for different reconstruction models to improve the privacy-utility tradeoff.
items.venue: ACM Workshop on Artificial Intelligence and Security (AISec)

items.title: Photovoltaic Modulation of MoS2 Transistors via Interfacial Photoelectron Injection in Pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN Heterostructures
items.abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor transistors offer attractive optoelectronic functionality beyond the scaling limits of conventional silicon technology. However, conventional 2D phototransistors often suffer from limited photoresponse performance, high energy consumption, and unstable threshold voltage. To overcome these challenges, we demonstrate a photovoltaic modulated field-effect transistor based on a pn-Si/MoS2/h-BN heterostructure. Under visible illumination, photogenerated electrons accumulate near the pn-Si/MoS2 interface and are vertically injected into the adjacent MoS2 conduction channel. A current change from approximately 3.8 μA to 11.2 μA is observed when illumination is switched on during a gate-voltage sweep, corresponding to a switching-event current ratio of approximately 2.95. Concurrently, the device exhibits reversible current modulation during the recorded optical ON/OFF cycles. Wavelength-dependent measurements further elucidate a critical competition between injection-driven carrier enhancement and high-field suppression effects. First-principles calculations using monolayer MoS2/h-BN heterostructure models further show that electron doping increases the electrical conductivity of MoS2 by increasing the occupation of conduction-band states and improving carrier transport. These results demonstrate optical modulation in Si-supported MoS2 devices and motivate further investigation of the contributions from interfacial carrier transfer and photovoltaic gating.

items.title: PadSink-Track: A Calibrated Framework for Padding-Sink-Preserving, Alignment-Tracked Selective Cross-Attention Key–Value Cache Access in CPU-Based Whisper Speech Recognition
items.abstract: To generate each token, the Whisper decoder re-reads the encoder’s 1500-position cross-attention key–value (KV) cache on the CPU. In the Whisper-medium model, this cache occupies 281 MiB; for short recordings, 74–82% of it consists of padding positions. This paper proposes a calibratable framework that reduces the number of KV positions read at each step without retraining the model or changing the cache kept in memory. The saving therefore comes from reading fewer bytes from DRAM at each step. Its core method—PadSink-Track—preserves critical “padding-sink” positions, shifts the audio window at each step based on signals from Whisper’s alignment heads, and updates selected KV entries in a ring buffer. A fallback mechanism re-executes the step using the full cache when confidence is low. The budget, sink fraction, and fallback threshold (τ) are calibrated for each model on a validation set based on a specified non-inferiority criterion (δ = 0.2 × WER). When the calibrated budget was halved, none of the selection rules relying solely on the first step met the criterion. In contrast, the calibrated framework satisfied this criterion across all ten configurations, covering four languages (Uzbek, English, Russian, Turkish) and two model sizes. On the held-out sets, every no-fallback decision was reproduced, and the single fallback decision (medium/English) became “Inconclusive”. In three configurations, where 19–35% of the steps were re-executed, the speed condition selected the full cache. On the Intel Core i7-11850H processor, decoder-step time without fallback decreased by 32–34% (synthetic step; 23–25% with real decoding), the volume of data read from DRAM dropped by 36–40%, and the throughput of the eight parallel decoders increased by 53% (synthetic step; 33% with real decoding, median latency −26%). Time savings during whole-utterance decoding amounted to 13–14% for models without fallback, whereas for the original medium model that required fallback, this figure was approximately 4%.

items.title: Orthogonally regulated multi-timescale reservoir and linear nonvolatile readout in a vertical transistor for dynamic machine vision
items.abstract: Abstract Implementing analog reservoir computing (RC) at the edge is fundamentally constrained by conflicting hardware requirements for the reservoir (volatile, nonlinear) and readout (nonvolatile, linear) layers. Here, we resolve this dilemma by monolithically integrating a multi-timescale photoelectric reservoir and a linear ferroelectric readout within a single vertical organic field-effect transistor (Fe-vOFET). This architecture functionally decouples photocarrier dynamics from ferroelectric polarization, allowing orthogonal optimization of reservoir dynamics and synaptic weights. In the optical mode, the Rubrene/F 16 CuPc heterojunction underpins reservoir dynamics, exploiting wavelength-dependent relaxation kinetics to construct multi-timescale grouped reservoirs that project inputs into high-dimensional spatiotemporal states. Conversely, in the electrical mode, the metal–ferroelectric–metal–insulator–semiconductor (MFMIS) stack governs readout functionality by mitigating interface trapping, translating remnant polarization into linear, symmetric, nonvolatile weight updates (endurance >10 6 , retention >3000 s, asymmetry nonlinearity 0.31 ± 0.05). The vertical-channel geometry is pivotal, simultaneously amplifying optical feedback and boosting the on/off ratio to ~10 7 , which is essential for high-fidelity weight mapping. Leveraging this dual-mode operation, we demonstrate a compact RC system achieving >90% accuracy in dynamic human-action recognition. This work establishes a scalable device paradigm that unifies dynamical richness with programming precision, paving the way for energy-efficient, all-in-one dynamic machine vision systems.

items.title: Neuromorphic Training of VO 2 Device at Behavioral Timescale Inspired by the Plasticity of CA1 Neurons of Live Mouse Brain
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing biologically relevant plasticity rules in hardware is a central goal in neuromorphic computing. This work demonstrates that an individual vanadium dioxide device exhibits features analogous to behavioral timescale synaptic plasticity observed in CA1 neurons of freely moving mice. By positioning the device close to the phase‐transition boundary, the history‐dependent dynamics of these VO 2 devices were leveraged to induce long‐lasting, pulse‐driven changes in conductance. A direct comparison with whole‐cell recordings from CA1 neurons in freely moving mice reveals that VO 2 channels exhibit plasticity‐like state changes after a strong input, suggesting an analog to plasticity induction in the brain. These results highlight VO 2 as a material platform capable of reproducing key temporal features of biologically relevant plasticity, suggesting a path toward neuromorphic hardware that more faithfully mirrors the adaptive capabilities of neural circuits in mammalian brains.

items.title: Nanoscale thickness engineering of Y2O3 Carrier-Modulation layer for Simultaneous contact and reliability improvement in Sol-Gel processed crystalline In2O3/Y2O3 heterostructure transistors
items.abstract: High-mobility In 2 O 3 channel thin-film transistors (TFTs) are promising for emerging electronics, but simultaneously achieving desirable contact properties and stable operation remains challenging. We demonstrate that nanoscale thickness engineering of the Y 2 O 3 carrier-modulation layer (CML) optimizes contact performance and current-stress reliability in crystalline In 2 O 3 /Y 2 O 3 heterostructure TFTs. Transmission line measurements show that the CML thickness (t CML ) governs width-normalized contact resistance (R C W) and effective channel-length deviation (ΔL), with ΔL strongly suppressed at higher t CML . Under positive-bias stress (PBS), the threshold-voltage shift (ΔV TH ) decreases from 2.06 V at t CML = 1.0 nm to 0.58–0.80 V at t CML = 2.5–10.0 nm. Under current stress (CS), a thickness-dependent failure path appears. Although t CML = 2.5–5.0 nm maintains a low ΔV TH (0.75 V), t CML = 10.0 nm uniquely develops pronounced hump formation and severe μ lin degradation, along with non-monotonic maximum transconductance evolution. Systematic stress testing and electrical parameter analysis revealed that sustained current flow triggers stress-induced leakage current and percolation-assisted parasitic conduction, manifesting as an anomalous hump and trap-assisted soft-breakdown that may evolve into time-dependent dielectric breakdown. Overall, these results establish a practical nanoscale thickness window for CML design and emphasize the importance of considering CS for stable heterostructure TFT operation.

items.title: Multichannel Phonon Interconversion Drives 90 Polarization Rotation for Stable Domain Walls in Hafnium Oxide
items.abstract: Polarization rotation is a fundamental mechanism in ferroelectric materials, yet how such rotation arises microscopically in fluorite ferroelectrics and gives rise to distinct domain walls (DW) remains unresolved. Phonon modes offer a microscopic route to such structural transformations, as geometric orientations can modify their frequencies, dispersion relations, and vibrational eigenstates when their characteristic wavelengths become comparable to relevant physical dimensions. Here, by combining condensed phonon mode decomposition with first-principles calculations, we investigate the origin of 90 polarization rotation in the ferroelectric phase of HfO2. Using the cubic parent phase as reference, we show that polarization rotation originates from multiple symmetry equivalent phonon modes of distinct eigenstates at different wavevectors in the Brillouin zone, whose coupling and cooperative reorientation continuously evolve to generate distinct 90 Pca21 variants and switching pathways. Among the 90 variants, the lowest-energy switching pathway through the Pmn21 exhibits an energy barrier comparable to, but slightly lower than, that of the 180 polarization reversal pathway through the P42/nmc phase, indicating that 90 polarization rotation is an energetically accessible alternative switching route. We further analyze 90 DW and find that frustrated phonon modes emerge at the wall center, where the coexistence and competition of condensed modes promote local reconfiguration of the lattice distortions, contributing to the elevated DW energies. Importantly, experimental observations with STEM imaging provide direct evidence of atomic mode distortions in stable 90 DW, consistent with the theoretically identified low-energy DW. These findings provide the fundamental structural mechanism underlying 90 switching dynamics, competing domain-wall physics, and macroscopic ferroelectric behavior.

items.title: Mitigating Sequence-of-Returns Risk with Regime-Switching Asset Allocation: A Comparison of Econometric and Deep Learning Models in Portfolio Decumulation
items.abstract: Abstract Retirement portfolios under regular withdrawals face sequence-of-returns risk: early losses can exhaust capital even when average returns are adequate. We examine whether regime-switching dynamic asset allocation mitigates this risk for a 60/40 stock-bond portfolio, and whether deep learning identifies regimes better than classical econometrics. Five models (a Markov-switching model, a multivariate and a univariate Gaussian hidden Markov model, an LSTM, and an encoder-only Transformer) are compared under identical data, tuning, and walk-forward validation. Their signals, net of transaction costs, feed 10{,}000 stationary-bootstrap retirement paths in three withdrawal scenarios. At 4.0% the MSM, the univariate HMM, and the LSTM cut the depletion rate from 3.30% to 0.57%, 0.60%, and 0.60% with disjoint Wilson intervals; at 6.0% only the LSTM reduces it (17.01% against 33.04%), the univariate filters raising it to about 49% as their return sacrifice becomes the dominant ruin cause, and the multivariate HMM raising it in every scenario. Only the econometric models turn defensive in all five crisis windows; neither network identifies regimes more accurately, and the LSTM holds the highest median terminal capital by staying invested rather than by timing regimes. Classification quality and search diagnostics do not predict decumulation value. Regime-switching allocation in decumulation is a state-contingent tail hedge: model choice determines the protected risk profile, and above a critical withdrawal rate the premium exceeds the payout.

items.title: Microelectronics Assembly and Packaging: Materials and Technologies, 2nd Edition
items.abstract: This Reprint collected 10 outstanding peer-reviewed articles, which focused on the materials and technologies of microelectronics assembly and packaging. The content of these articles was within the scope of the Special Issue. For example, the assessment of crack formation at a hybrid bonding interface was reported; interposer-based ESD protection was found to be a potential solution for μ-packaging reliability of 3D chips; interconnects’ resonance and signal/power integrity degradation in glass packages were measured and analyzed; the impact of bonding pressure on reactive bonding was explored; post-wire-bonding corrosion prevention strategies were proposed to mitigate Chloride- and Bromide-induced corrosion failures in Cu- and PCC-based wire-bonded packages; etc. Any readers whose interests are within the aforementioned areas, we welcome you to read this Reprint.

items.title: Learning to remember: advances in memory mechanisms for large language models
items.abstract: Abstract Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations, or model weights; and memory for agent evolution, where stored experiences support reinforcement learning, continual learning, procedural reuse, context engineering, and agent harness design. Evaluation is treated as a separate cross-cutting component rather than as a memory mechanism. Unlike surveys that focus primarily on retrieval-augmented generation or long-context modeling, this paper emphasizes the full memory life cycle: construction, maintenance, retrieval, consolidation, forgetting, governance, and evaluation. By aligning conceptual motivations, computational memory mechanisms, benchmarks, and deployment concerns, the survey provides a structured roadmap for designing memory-augmented LLM agents that are persistent, adaptive, auditable, and safe to update over time.

items.title: Large Language Models in Museum Communication: Opportunities, Risks, and Implementation Requirements
items.abstract: The transition of museum institutions into the era of generative artificial intelligence is characterized by systemic transformation, from the representation of digitized collections to dynamic interaction within a synthetic digital environment. Under these conditions, the challenge of adapting traditional standards of museum authenticity to the stochastic nature of large language models (LLMs) becomes particularly pressing. This study aims to develop a conceptual understanding of the transformation of museum communication, identify the epistemological challenges posed by the algorithmic generation of context and meaning, and describe mechanisms for preserving institutional authority as neural network–based tools are integrated into the public sphere. The study draws on a synthesis of institutional and communication approaches, which makes it possible to consider the museum not only as a custodian of material heritage but also as an active mediator amid increasing information noise. The empirical basis of the study consists of an analysis of the practical and educational agenda of the Hermitage School of Communication, held in Petrozavodsk in September 2025. The methodology involved identifying the professional competencies required to work in a hybrid media environment and evaluating practical applications of media analytics carried out by museum professionals using readily available AI tools designed for end users. The findings indicate that the adoption of LLMs inevitably shifts the focus of museum work away from routine content creation toward critical verification, strategic planning, and the management of meaning-making narratives. The stochastic nature of these models was found to give rise to risks of semantic uncertainty, including the loss of historical context, the reproduction of latent biases, and the substitution of factual information with probabilistic constructs. At the same time, the study illustrates the high effectiveness of algorithms in media analytics tasks, such as clustering audience inquiries and identifying latent patterns in unstructured feedback data. A key determinant of success is not only the model's technological capabilities but also the quality of research design established by the specialist when formulating the prompt. The findings point to the need to reconsider assumptions about the extent to which intellectual work in the cultural sector can be automated. An approach is proposed in which AI operates within bounded environments of verified museum data. The need for museums to adapt their infrastructure is also highlighted, including the creation of secure digital corpora, the implementation of transparent protocols for labeling synthetic content, and the development of ethical principles. The study emphasizes that, in the era of synthetic communication, the critical thinking and in-depth expertise of museum professionals remain particularly valuable resources.

items.title: La Vattiata, Federico; Kenyon, Tony; Lombardo, Antonio; Wallis, Kate; (2026) Regulating Neuromorphic Computing in the UK: An application-led framework for brain-inspired Technologies
items.abstract: Emerging technologies are difficult to regulate because their capabilities, uses and even basic boundaries can change quickly, and develop faster than regulators' understanding and existing regulatory frameworks.This creates a difficult policy challenge: regulators must protect the public from potential harms without unnecessarily constraining innovation.Where regulation fails to keep pace, significant harms may fall through regulatory gaps.At the same time, where regulation is introduced without a clear understanding of the technology or its risks, it may impose unnecessary burdens on beneficial innovation.Neuromorphic computing (NC) illustrates this challenge particularly well because its technical boundaries remain fluid and its applications can create very different risks.Neuromorphic systems may combine hardware-dependent processing, edge deployment, real-time operation, and adaptation after deployment.These characteristics challenge assumptions underlying existing approaches to regulating emerging technology, including how countries currently approach artificial intelligence (AI) governance.1,2,3,4 What is neuromorphic computing?Neuromorphic computing is a family of braininspired technologies.The term encompasses different combinations of hardware, software, sensors and braininspired computing methods, and the field remains at an early stage of development.These systems aim to make computing more energy-efficient, responsive, and capable of processing information closer to where it is generated.Potential applications include autonomous vehicles, medical devices, industrial systems and defence.However, NC is not a single, clearly bounded technology.

items.title: Interface‐Mediated Self‐Rectifying CsCuCl 3 Memristors With Tunable Thresholds for Reconfigurable Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: ABSTRACT We demonstrate a simple 1R self‐rectifying halide perovskite memristor with dynamically tunable thresholds for selector‐free crossbar arrays and programmable T‐ReLU mapping. The memristors achieve an ON/OFF ratio > 10 5 and rectification ratio > 10 4 . The switching mechanism involves two synergistic processes: bulk ion migration within CsCuCl 3 provides and sustains the low‐resistance state essential for a high ON/OFF ratio, while the Ag‐Cl‐containing oxidized interfacial layer introduces a Schottky barrier and trap filling/release mechanism that governs the HRS to LRS switching. Systematic simulations using CNN architectures reveal a dataset‐dependent threshold sensitivity: MNIST accuracy remains robust (> 98%) regardless of threshold variations, whereas CIFAR‐10 accuracy drops sharply as positive thresholds increase. Based on this complexity‐dependent trend, we exploited the bi‐directional tunability for dual‐mode applications: (i) Negative threshold operation in CNNs maintains 91.0% accuracy for low‐light image recognition (comparable to the ReLU baseline); (ii) Positive threshold modulation in a customized SparseResNet‐18 architecture is explored for sparsity‐aware edge computing, where thresholds τ ∈ [0, 0.3] are adjusted according to simulated battery levels to control the sparsity‐accuracy trade‐off. Under low‐battery conditions (τ = 0.3), the simulated network achieves 76.3% activation sparsity while maintaining 90.1% accuracy without retraining. This work highlights the potential of tunable activation thresholds for reconfigurable neuromorphic systems.

items.title: Influence of epitaxial strain on structural relaxation in crystalline membranes of fluorite oxides
items.abstract: Using synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we investigated how epitaxial strain influences structural relaxation in freestanding crystalline membranes of fluorite oxides. When epitaxial films of yttrium-doped hafnium oxide Hf0.93Y0.07O2(HYO) with the metastable orthorhombic phase under compressive strain were exfoliated from La0.7Sr0.3MnO3(LSMO)-buffered (110) SrTiO3 substrates, the strain was partially relaxed, while the metastable phase was preserved in the membrane form. In contrast, the metastable orthorhombic phase of zirconium dioxide (ZrO2) films grown on (110) LSMO/STO substrates and under negligibly small strain underwent structural relaxation into the thermodynamically stable monoclinic phase upon exfoliation from the substrate. These results indicate that the energy barrier between the metastable orthorhombic phase and the monoclinic one is less for ZO than for HYO, highlighting that the stability of the metastable phase, which is modulated by the strain, influences the structural relaxation in fluorite oxide membranes.
items.venue: Science and Technology of Advanced Materials

items.title: Impact of a process-induced interfacial layer on ferroelectric switching and reliability in AlScN/ β -Ga2O3 MFS capacitors
items.abstract: In this study, we demonstrate AlScN-based metal–ferroelectric–semiconductor capacitors directly integrated on a heteroepitaxial β-Ga2O3. Structural analysis reveals the presence of a process-induced amorphous intermixed layer at the AlScN/β-Ga2O3 interface. The fabricated devices exhibit ferroelectric switching behavior, characterized by counterclockwise hysteretic current–voltage loops with an on/off current ratio of >102, which is limited by the intermixed interfacial layer. Piezo-response force microscopy measurements confirm the intrinsic polarization switching capability through phase reversal and butterfly-shaped amplitude loops. Furthermore, positive-up-negative-down measurements indicate polarization switching while revealing a switching current asymmetry. We identify that this asymmetry originates from the internal electric field and charge trapping associated with the interfacial defect layer. This interfacial instability primarily affects the device performance observed during retention (103 s) and endurance (5 × 103 cycles) tests, suggesting significance of the interface toward stable ferroelectric operation in AlScN/β-Ga2O3 devices.

items.title: HyperMesh-512: Hyper-Parallel Inference Acceleration Architecture for Massive Language Models Based on a 2D Mesh NoC and a Decentralized 32-Channel LPDDR4X/DDR4 Bus
items.abstract: HyperMesh-512 is a hyper-parallel PCIe inference accelerator architecture engineered to overcome the Memory Wall bottleneck during autoregressive decoding of massive language models (such as Llama 3.1 70B/405B and DeepSeek-R1/V3 671B MoE). Featuring 512 GB of commodity LPDDR4X/DDR4 memory distributed across 32 independent physical 64-bit point-to-point channels coupled to 16 ASIC micro-chiplets in a 2D Mesh NoC (X-Y DOR routing), the board delivers 819.2 GB/s to 1,092.1 GB/s of sustained memory bandwidth. To address ultra-long context windows (≥ 128k tokens), each chiplet integrates a dedicated single-cycle affine INT4 to INT16 hardware decompressor, reducing 128k KV-cache footprint from 41.94 GB down to 10.49 GB and raising effective context read bandwidth to 3,276.8 GB/s equivalent. Audited Industrial BOM: US$ 1,680.00. Target MSRP: US$ 4,999.00 delivering 102.42 GB/k$ (a 48x capital-efficiency advantage over corporate HGX H100 clusters), with a 98.33% CapEx reduction and 96.57% electrical OpEx reduction for on-premise, air-gapped private generative AI workloads. Declaração de Natureza Teórica: Artigo teórico / preprint técnico contendo modelagem arquitetural, RTL sintetizável e projeções tecno-econômicas. Propriedade Intelectual e Licenciamento (Royalties): Titularidade de Tiago Barbosa Dias Maciel (CPF 060.184.906-09, tiago@brmg.com.br). Qualquer exploração comercial sujeita a licenciamento e royalty de US$ 50,00 por placa ou US$ 3,00 por chiplet integrado.
items.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Hardware reconfigurable secure data acquisition system of a shared ADC in heterogenous multi-channel inputs with automatic sampling frequency configurations
items.abstract: Abstract Multi-channel Data Acquisition (DAQ) Systems can use a single multiplexed analog to digital converter (ADC) to reduce system cost. But this ADC must be configured to proper sampling rate for each channel. In this paper, a novel algorithm is proposed to automatically generate ADC configuration, and improve the ADC’s utilization and utility, reduce the number of redundant bits, and reduce cost. This proposed algorithm is mathematically formulated, and numerical examples are given. The research methodology involves using FPGA board with analog to digital and digital to analog conversion card, and synthetic wave form is generated and captured for verification. In this phase, a single channel is investigated, as the investigation of multi-channel DAQ requires the integration and scheduling of the ADC with an external analog multiplexer. In prior work, a custom computer board is designed to implement the HTMS algorithm for 32 analog channels. To effectively demonstrate the previously proposed HTMS superiority against other approaches, new performance metrics were defined, namely the ADC’s utilization, utility and efficiency using two different heuristic analog input sets. These metrics show that the HTMS-based DAQ outperforms relevant systems as it reaches 100% of ADC’s utilization and utility, while other systems have 75% utilization, and 6.25% utility. By devising a unified figure of merit for multiple DAQ systems, it is shown that the proposed system is higher by 218% compared to the baseline multi-channel DAQ system. Furthermore, Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) has been extensively investigated for cryptographic applications. A given pipelined 54-cycle AES-256-bit key core is considered for enhancement. With a single cycle design approach, the given core is successfully implemented in FPGA device using only 14-cycles / round, and generating a maximum encryption throughput of 12.8 Gb/s, with an FPGA utilization of only 9% Cyclone V SX SoC 5CSXFC6D6F31C6N, with speed up factor of 7 times is reported, compared to recent results, operating at a maximum clock frequency of 100 MHz.
